# Charter
In compliance with the newly approved City Ordinance No. 1, Series of 2025, which officially supersedes City Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2018, Gordon College affirms its full adherence to the updated directives as mandated by the local government. The institution remains committed to aligning its policies and operations with the latest regulatory framework to ensure a lawful, effective, and community-responsive higher educational institution.

# College Seal
This is the official college seal/logo of Gordon College. This is to be used in legal and formal documents and correspondence of the College. The colors green and yellow signify the community college’s commitment to sustainable development or a development for all generations as it works towards environmental sustainability in its attainment of its vision, mission and goals. “Ulo ng Apo” represents the city of Olongapo where the local Higher Education Institution is based. This symbolizes the ability of its students to lead and make a difference in the community.
The torch illuminates a book which represents the ability to serve as a guiding light for others. It also shows how education is a beacon of light that nurture learning. It is strategically placed beneath the Ulo ng Apo signifying that knowledge must be used, not for knowledge’s sake, but more for the community which includes its stakeholders.
The circular wreath made of interlocking branches and leaves represents the unity and strength of stakeholders and its students who stand among the distinguished scholars the local HEI molded and developed. With the wreath of laurel leaves being a symbol of honor and victory, students, faculty and the leaders of the institution are expected to achieve victory over ignorance while remaining honorable and preserving integrity towards excellence.
The platinum colored shield placed behind the Ulo ng Apo represents the boldness of its students in pursuit of new horizons of unparalleled intellectual success. To remind its students staff and all the members of the institution to be bold and brave enough to explore and seek new opportunities beyond the four corners of the college towards the development of the community they belong to.
Under the shield is the year that Gordon College was founded. This represents the number of years of upholding its values. Three values guide the college, namely: excellence; character and service which shall guide the institutions’ trifocal function of instruction, research and extension.
The logo is in a form of circle, symbolizing the perfect fulfillment of a holistic educational process.

# History of Gordon College
Gordon College was an off-shoot of the Olongapo City Training Center, then a training center for skilled manpower for employment at the former Naval facility of the United States. With the facility’s closure, and the slowing down of demand for skilled workers, City residents shifted to professional courses. The unavailability of affordable tertiary institutions for urban poor sector of the population led the City Government of Olongapo, during the incumbency of Hon. Katherine H. Gordon, then City Mayor, to open the Olongapo City Colleges through City Ordinance no. 9 series of 1999.
Initially, the College offered Bachelor of Science in Accountancy and Bachelor of Science in Computer Studies to 177 enrollees. Additional four-year programs were offered in the succeeding years to accommodate the demand of City residents for other programs.
City Ordinance no. 42 series of 2002 was passed in May 2002, providing a change in the name of Olongapo City Colleges to Gordon College, its present name, in honor of the Gordon family who greatly contributed to the development of the City of Olongapo. In the same year, the College was officially accepted as a member of the Association of Local Colleges and Universities (ALCU).
In 2004, a revision on the legal basis for the creation and operation of Gordon College was made through City Ordinance no. 36 series of 2004. In the same year, the College was granted by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Region III the certificate to operate with autonomy as per provisions of the Local Government Code of 19991. In addition to its undergraduate programs, the College opened its graduate programs in Education, Public Management and Business Administration.
In 2018, City Ordinance No. 07 series of 2018 was passed revising the charter of Gordon College subject to all Legal and Existing Rules and Regulations. This was superseded by City Ordinance No. 01 series of 2025 which was passed in 2025 that equipped Gordon College to expand its horizon for excellence to national and international level.

# Mandate and Function
Gordon College, formerly Olongapo City Colleges, is a local higher education institution established in 1999 under the City Government of Olongapo.
The College operates by virtue of City Ordinance No. 36, Series of 2004 and its amendment City Ordinance No. 1, Series of 2025 also known as the “ 2025 Revised Charter of Gordon College” that supersedes the City Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2018 . The proposed revision of the Charter of Gordon College aims to strengthen the promotion of excellence and delivery of education in the national and international level.
The Local Government of Olongapo supports and maintains its commitment to provide accessible and equitable distribution of opportunities to its constituents to acquire higher education, as well as, a responsive and relevant higher education institution.
### Legal Bases
* **CHED Memorandum Order No. 32, Series of 2006** – Policies, Standards and Guidelines on the Establishment and Operation of Local Colleges and Universities (LCUs);
* **CHED Memorandum Order No. 4, Series of 2007** – Implementing Rules of CM032, Series of 2006;
* **CHED Memorandum Order No. 42, Series of 2016** – Amendment of Article V, Section 5 and 12 of CMO 32, Series of 2006;
* **DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2009-67** – Guidelines on the Establishment of Local Colleges and Universities by Local Governments, and on the Operation of Higher Education Programs;
* **Republic Act No. 7722** – Higher Education Act of 1994;
* **Republic Act No. 9160** – Local Government code of 1991;
* **City Ordinance No. 1, Series of 2025** – 2025 Revised Charter of Gordon College
* **City Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2018** – Revised Charter of Gordon College of 2018;
* **City Ordinance No. 8, Series of 2010** – An Ordinance Amending the Legal Basis on the Creation and Operation of Gordon College;
* **Resolution No. 42, Series of 2002**– A Resolution Chaning the Name of Olongapo City Colleges to “Gordon College”;
* **City Ordinance No. 9, Series of 1999** – An Ordinance Creating Olongapo City Colleges

# Vision, Mission, Objectives, and Core Values
## Vision
A globally recognized local institution committed to innovative academic excellence, holistic and sustainable development, inclusivity, and community engagement.
## Mission
Produce empowered global citizens who create sustainable impact, uphold values of character, excellence, and service, and contribute to academic and societal development
## Strategic Objectives
1. **H**arness partnerships and linkages to produce graduates with global competencies aligned with the needs of the community and industry.
2. **O**rganize extension programs to sustain the greater impact of the institution to the community and environment.
3. **L**everage research outputs to improve existing knowledge and practices.
4. **I**ntegrate ethical principles and standards in the curriculum to strengthen the moral responsibilities of lifelong learners.
5. **S**upport continuous professional development and well-being of employees.
6. **T**ailor-fit student support services to ensure students thrive in the rapidly changing world.
7. **I**nvest in state-of-the-art facilities and technologies to enhance teaching, learning and research.
8. **C**ultivate a culture that embraces diversity and inclusivity.
## Core Values
* **Character.** Character is the foundation of a meaningful life. The institution strives to instill in students a strong moral compass, integrity, and a sense of responsibility for their actions. This includes fostering critical thinking skills, respect for diversity, and a commitment to a lifelong learning.
* **Excellence.** The institution provides a rigorous academic environment that challenges students to reach their full potential. Intellectual curiosity, innovation, and a pursuit of knowledge for its won sake is encouraged. It is believed that excellence is not just about achieving high grades, but also about developing the ability to analyze complex problems, think creatively, and communicate effectively.
* **Service.** Education empowers individuals to make a positive impact on their communities and the world. Students are encouraged to engage in service-learning opportunities that allow them to apply their knowledge and skills to real-world problems. The institution fosters a culture of social responsibility where students develop a sense of compassion and a desire to contribute to the betterment of society.

# Colleges
**Institute of Graduate Studies**
The mission of the Institute of Graduate Studies of Gordon College is to provide quality master’s degree programs and opportunities for continuing professional and career development for students whose academic preparation and personal characteristics foresee success in graduate studies. Each graduate program is firmly grounded in theoretical and empirical bodies of knowledge. Students are challenged to think critically and creatively, and to apply theories to practice in an atmosphere of inquiry and dynamic exchange with faculty and each other
**College of Allied Health Studies**
By 2025, the College of Allied Health Studies is envisioned to be a Center of Excellence in Allied Health Education in Region III and dedicated to being a forerunner in providing research-inclined instruction, evidence-based practice and community–responsive health care education committed to the holistic development of the human person.
**College of Business and Accountancy**
A center of excellence in accounting and business education that develops competitive leaders and professionals for providing professional training, innovative research and relevant extension services.
**College of Computer Studies**
The College of Computer Studies shall be the Center of Excellence in Information Technology and Computer Science for providing professional and technological training, scientific and innovative, and relevant community service
**College of Education, Arts and Sciences**
We envision the Gordon College-College of Education, Arts and Sciences to be a center of excellence in the field for providing professional training, innovative research and community service.
**College of Hospitality and Tourism Management**
To be a center of excellence in tourism and hospitality management with high standard through instruction, research and extension.

# Academic Affairs
Academic affairs is the institutional office that oversees a variety of academic programs and departments at a school. The head of this office supports curriculum initiatives, faculty hiring and promotion events, faculty research and teaching, and all academic departments and programs.

# Continuing Students, Returnees and Cross Enrollment
## Continuing Students and Returnees
Continuing students are those who were previously enrolled in the College but unable to enroll for at least one semester and decided to continue studying in GC. These students have not requested for any transfer credential. They may have or have not filed for Leave of Absence.
Returning students are those who requested for transfer credentials but decided to re-enroll in the College. Returning students shall no longer be required to take the admission test.
## Cross Enrollment
* **GC Students to Enroll in Other Schools**
  + Students shall not be allowed to cross-enroll without proper consultation and consent from their respective College Deans. Students shall not be allowed to cross-enroll if the subject/course is not open during his/her last two semesters in the College. He/She shall request recommendation from his/her Dean and authorization coming from the College Registrar before he/she can cross-enroll to other colleges/universities.
* **Students from Other Schools to Cross-enroll in GC**
  + Students from other schools who would cross-enroll in GC should present a written permission from his school that he/she is allowed to enroll in GC.

# Freshmen Students
## Admission Requirements
Admission to Gordon College shall be open to Filipino citizens, both residents and non-residents of Olongapo City, Non-Filipino citizens, high school graduates, or passers of the high school equivalency certificate (PEPT), and shows evidence of being able to benefit from instruction. A NON-RESIDENT is defined as any individual who has lived less than one year in Olongapo City, is not registered to vote in Olongapo City and/or does not pay property taxes or contributes to the economic development of Olongapo City.
## New College Freshmen Students for Undergraduate Programs
* Admission to the chosen degree program will be based on an applicant’s Gordon College Admission Test (GCAT) results and previous high school/college academic records.
* Original copy of High School Report Card (F138/SF9) or Original ALS Certificate of Rating Secondary Level for ALS Passers
* Certificate of Good Moral Character
* Copy of Birth Certificate
* Medical Certificate (Issued by the Gordon College Clinic)
* Barangay Certificate of Residency
* One 2×2 picture

# IGS (Institute of Graduate Studies) Students
To qualify for admission to the Institute of Graduate Studies, an applicant must meet the following general and specific standards:
1. Student must have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 2.00 or 85% (except NSTP and PE). Student with lower general average than the prescribed rating may be admitted to the master’s program on probation. While on probationary status, s/he is allowed to carry the maximum load of only six (6) units per term. S/he will be placed in full standing status after having obtained an average rating of 1.5 or better in the first 12 units.
2. Specific programs may have different requirement as well as additional requirements such as materials and a personal interview, to wit:
   1. Master in Public Administration
      * At least two (2) years of government/ public service in any capacity
   2. Master in Business Management
      * BS Commerce or BS Business Administration graduate
      * Non-business course graduate must finish 18 tool courses. While earning these units, s/he may enroll any two basic/major subjects in the MBM program.
      * At least two (2) years of relevant experience/ service.
   3. Master of Arts in Education
      * Should be an education graduate
      * For non-education graduate, at least 24 units of professional education in the undergraduate level.
      * At least two (2) years of teaching experience/ service.
   4. Master of Arts in Nursing
      * Should be a Registered Nurse
      * At least two (2) years of experience in nursing and/or related field.
3. Pass the qualifying examination and interview.
4. All applicants for admission must submit the following;
   * Original Transcript of Records from recognized colleges or universities (with remarks, “Copy for Gordon College” or “Granted Honorable Dismissal”).
   * Two ID pictures (2×2/passport size)
   * Certificate of Employment
   * A Php200.00 non-refundable fee for application processing.
   * Additional materials, if required by specific program.

# Student Publication
**The Forefront** is the official student publication of Gordon College located in Olongapo City Sports Complex, Donor Street, East Tapinac, Olongapo City 2200. Its office is located at Rm. 516, 5th Floor, GC Main Building.
The Forefront was reestablished on June 2009, after a four-year hiatus, with the desire to promote the development and growth of responsible journalism as a means of strengthening ethical values, encouraging critical and creative thinking, and developing moral character and personal discipline in accordance with the Campus Journalism Act of 1991 (R.A. 7079).
**THE LOGO**
The official logo of the Forefront, as appeared above, is consist of two elements and two colors.
A *quill or pluma* refers to the writing profession. Its color, red, symbolizes courage and sacrifice. A *stem of laurel leaves* signifies triumph. Its color, golden yellow, symbolizes the nobility of the writing profession. The quill and the stem of laurel leaves form a capital letter “F” which stands for The Forefront.
**General Principles and Objectives**
The Forefront lives with its tagline, **“Informing and Empowering.”** To be able to uphold with its battlecry for campus press freedom, the Editorial Board sets the following General Principles:
1. The Forefront shall serve primarily as a newspaper of and for the students. It shall protect and promote the constitutionally mandated rights of students to free speech and of expression. In addition, it shall protect and promote the students’ rights and welfare.
2. The Forefront, being a publication of the students devoted to the ideals of truth, shall pursue the mission of social transformation through active and responsible journalism.
3. The Forefront, being an independent institution, shall not be subjected to any form of censorship. In turn, the editors and staff shall see to it that the Forefront exercises academic and campus press freedom in accordance with the laws of the Republic of the Philippines. It shall also seek to protect and promote  
   press freedom by taking firm and assertive stance against elements endangering such right.
4. The editors shall respect the rights of other parties that are equally protected by the laws of the Republic of the Philippines, affording them the right and opportunity to refute or reply to criticism or comment hurled at them.
Along with this principles, The Forefront shall at all times strive to:
1. Inform the public (i.e. the general population of the College, including the administration and the general public outside the College) with news of relevance and interest;
2. Serve as a venue for campus opinion and in maintaining an atmosphere of free and responsible discussion and of intellectual exploration;
3. Provide an outlet for students’ suggestions for the betterment of the campus;
4. Develop students’ powers of observation and discrimination concerning relative merits of news articles and;
5. Provide an opportunity for journalistic and creative writing.

# CEAS Pins 269 Pre-service Educators in 18th Convocation Ceremony
[Image: CEAS Pins 269 Pre-service Educators in 18th Convocation Ceremony]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, December 10, 2025**
SMX Convention Center — The College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS) marked a milestone in the journey of its future educators during the 18th Pinning and Candle Lighting Ceremony last December 3, Wednesday, as the student teachers became full fledged practice teachers.
This year’s cohort included a total of 269 student teachers across various programs: 22 from Bachelor of Culture and Arts Education (BCAEd), 17 from Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (BECED), 50 from Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEED), 42 from Bachelor of Physical Education (BPEd), and 138 from Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSEd) who are deployed in various public and private schools across Olongapo City.
In his welcome remarks, Dr. Darwin Paguio, OIC-Dean of the College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS), emphasized Gordon College’s commitment to transferring theory learned in the classroom onto the field. He highlighted how CEAS’s education programs ensure that every deployed student teacher is academically prepared within the “four corners of the classroom” and fully ready to apply these theories once they step into real teaching environments.
Following this is the ceremonial passing of the Torch and Book of Wisdom, carried by Mr. Kristoffer Obispo and Ms. Juanalyn Olaguer, respectively. “The torch has been an important symbol since early civilization,” said Dr. Catherine Mobo as the torch is lit, explaining that it embodies the “light of tomorrow” that educators carry into the lives of learners. Meanwhile, Ms. Agnes Melo presented the Book of Wisdom, reminding the future educators that “its pages hold not only theories but the hopes and futures of learners we are called to guide.”
Delivering the keynote speech, Ms. Ilynne Samonte, CESE, Assistant Schools Division Superintendent, shared five heartfelt “pabaon” from her own internship journey at Philippine Normal University (PNU). She shared lessons she hopes the student teachers will carry into their practicum from the significance of being on time to the importance of taking care of oneself.
She also reminded the attendees of their future roles in public service, expressing her confidence that many of the candidates would one day serve in the Department of Education: “Most of you, if not all of you, will join us at DepEd sooner or later… Sabi nga, hindi pwede ang ‘pwede na.’ Ultimately, that will be your contribution to your community and your country.”
The 269 student teachers were ceremoniously pinned by their guardians with an official teacher’s nameplate. Their designated resource teachers — tenured teachers in their deployed school who have guided them — also passed the flames of their candle onto the wicks of their student teacher’s candle.
Solemn tears were shed at SMX as an audio-visual presentation was shown with photos from their college journey set to Ben & Ben’s hit song “Saranggola”. “Sa’n man tayo hipan ng amihan, hindi ipagpapalit ang pagkakaibigan,” the song played as numerous iconic moments through the years flashed on screen.
Emotions further deepened as the student teachers sang a musical tribute of “MAPA” by SB19 as they gifted a rose to their parents whose support made the milestone possible.
The ceremony concluded with closing remarks from Mr. Samuel Felip D. Fastidio, Field Study Supervisor and Program Chair of the BPEd Program, who congratulated the candidates and encouraged them to carry their symbols—torch, book, and candle—with a purpose as they step into the teaching profession as Gordon College’s newest teaching interns.
After hours of classroom observation in their field study, the 269 student teachers who are deployed in various schools will now formally step into their practicum as they take over their respective school classrooms. | via Love Lorraine Acedo & Lance Isaac Leon, The FOREFRONT
Photos by Jasmine Shameer Bañaga

# GCAAI Unveils New Student Lounge at Gordon College
[Image: GCAAI Unveils New Student Lounge at Gordon College]
[Alumni](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/alumni/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, August 15, 2025**
GCAAI Unveils New Student Lounge at Gordon College
The Gordon College Alumni Association, Inc. (GCAAI) is proud to announce the official blessing and turnover of the new Gordon College Student Lounge. The lounge, a project lovingly referred to as the “Garden Project,” was blessed by Rev. Fr. Mike Duffin before being officially handed over to the college. This new space is for students, faculty, administration, alumni, and other members of the Gordon College community.
The initiative was spearheaded by Mr. Theo Roi N. Musni, GCAAI Public Information Officer, with the full support of Mr. Joseph Angelo B. Pusing, GCAAI President, the GCAAI Board of Trustees, GCAAI working committee members, the GC Board of Trustees headed by City Mayor Hon. Rolen C. Paulino Jr., officials headed by College President Dr. Imelda DP. Soriano, and all Gordon College alumni.
The blessing and turnover ceremony was attended by Dr. Imelda DP. Soriano, Gordon College President, along with the college’s Vice Presidents. This new lounge stands as a testament to the GCAAI’s commitment to giving back to its alma mater.

# Weave of Strenght: Turning Fabric Scraps into Sustainable Livelihoods
[Image: Weave of Strenght: Turning Fabric Scraps into Sustainable Livelihoods]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Thursday, April 23, 2026**
Weave of Strength: Turning Scraps into Sustainable Livelihood Orientation and Training was successfully conducted on April 22, 2026, at the Audio Visual Room (AVR) of Gordon College. The event served as an orientation and training session for administrative personnel, equipping them with the knowledge and skills needed to become future trainers for the program.  
The training was led by College President, Dr. Imelda DP. Soriano, who demonstrated technical weaving skills, proper tool handling, and safety practices, followed by the active participation of administrative personnel, including institutional staff, extension personnel, selected faculty members, person with disabilities (PWD) and single parents.  
This initiative was made possible through the support of the Rotary Club of Downtown Olongapo, the DEI (Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Unit), the RDCES (Research Development and Community Extension Services), and in collaboration with the College of Hospitality and Tourism Management, further strengthening its goal of promoting sustainability, skills development, and community empowerment by transforming fabric scraps into meaningful livelihood opportunities.

# GC Welcomes 5 new Registered Midwifes, Perfect passing in November MLE
[Image: GC Welcomes 5 new Registered Midwifes, Perfect passing in November MLE]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, November 19, 2025**
Five alumni from the College of Allied Health and Services (CAHS) of Gordon College (GC) passed the Midwives Licensure Exam (MLE) according to the Professional Regulation Commission Board.
GC achieved a perfect passing rate of 100% with 5 passers out of 5 examinees, once again surpassing the rate of last year’s results of 93.48% and the national rate of 57.60%. They constitute the 2,152 newly registered midwives.
All are first-time takers of this year’s exam.
Additionally, Tagaloan Community College is the top-performing school in the licensure exam with a perfect passing rate from 85 examinees of the school.
Meanwhile, Princesa Dumale Talamayan, this year’s board topnotcher, from Palawan State University achieved a 94.00%.
The licensure exam was held on November 8-9 and 16. | via Roi Chester B. Manio/The FOREFRONT

# Beauty Meets Sportsmanship: Pislaan and Pradas Crowned as Mr. and Ms. Sportsfest 2025
[Image: Beauty Meets Sportsmanship: Pislaan and Pradas Crowned as Mr. and Ms. Sportsfest 2025]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Monday, September 15, 2025**
GORDON COLLEGE, OLONGAPO CITY— Cheers filled the East Tapinac Oval Grounds as the perfect blend of charm and athletic spirit came to life with representatives from various colleges showcasing their poise and sportsmanship, on the recently concluded Mr. and Ms. Sportsfest 2025 on Monday, September 15.
Kick-starting off the event with a bang, representatives wowed the crowd with their charisma and creative display of athletic-themed fashion for the Best in Sportswear award, which went to Mr. Chester Pislaan and Ms. Bhavjeet Kaur L. Singh from the College of Education, Arts and Sciences (CEAS) Mentors.
But the night didn’t end there—the battle for the ultimate title pushed the candidates to bring out their best poise, personality, and confidence. As the event drew to a close, the stage erupted in cheers and anticipation as the overall winners were finally announced.
After an intense showdown, Ms. Dhana Del C. Pradas from the College of Business and Accountancy (CBA) Wizards and Mr. Chester Pislaan from the College of Education, Arts and Sciences (CEAS) emerged as Mr. and Ms. Sportsfest—proving that talent, wit, and stage presence shine brightest when matched with determination and sportsmanship.
Furthermore, hot on their heels, the 1st Runner-Up titles went to Mr. Marc Anthony Acula (CBA) Wizards and Ms. Bhavjeet Kaur L. Singh (CEAS) Mentors, whose outstanding performances made them strong contenders throughout the competition.
Meanwhile, Mr. Krizztan Vic A. Dominico and Ms. Ron Eriele Joi P. Agustin from College of Allied Health Studies (CAHS) Tigers secured the 2nd Runner-Up spot, earning admiration for their dynamic partnership.
In 3rd place, Mr. Charles De Leon from College of Computer Studies (CCS) Phoenix and Ms. Alexandra Macky Alisbo from College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) claimed their rightful spot. At the same time, Mr. Jack Francis P. Meran (CHTM) Sharks and Ms. Janna Lyn Rolls, CCS Phoenix, completed the roster as the 4th place finishers. | via Love Lorainne Venus Acedo/The FOREFRONT

# Blessing of Gordon College Annex Building
[Image: Blessing of Gordon College Annex Building]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Monday, August 11, 2025**
Pormal na binasbasan ang bagong Annex Building ng Gordon College ngayong Agosto 11, 2025, sa pangunguna ni Rev. Fr. Roque Villanueva.
Dumalo sa makabuluhang seremonya sina Mayor Atty. Rolen C. Paulino Jr., BCDA Director Rolen C. Paulino, Gordon College President Dr. Imelda D.P. Soriano, mga Konsehal ng Lungsod, at ilan pang opisyal, kasama ang mga estudyante, guro, at kawani ng Gordon College bilang pagsuporta sa makasaysayang pagbubukas ng bagong gusali.
Mahigit sa tatlong libong karagdagang estudyante ang makikinabang sa bagong gusali.
Itinakda ang pagbubukas ng Annex Building kasabay ng pasimula ng klase ngayong Academic Year 2025–2026, bilang bahagi ng patuloy na pagtugon ng lokal na pamahalaan at pamunuan ng kolehiyo sa lumalaking pangangailangan para sa dekalidad at makabagong pasilidad sa edukasyon.

# TF’s Luto, among top newsletters at 2026 AOCPA; scribes bag 4 individual awards
[Image: TF’s Luto, among top newsletters at 2026 AOCPA; scribes bag 4 individual awards]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, March 7, 2026**
he Forefront, the official student publication of Gordon College, took home the 8th Most Outstanding Campus Newsletter and four individual awards at the 6th Assumption Outstanding Campus Press Awards (AOCPA).
The event, hosted by the University of the Assumption’s Regina, took place in San Fernando, Pampanga, on February 27.
The first semestral issue of The Forefront, Luto, was one of this year’s recipients of Most Outstanding Campus Newsletter.
During the awards ceremony, the publication’s Editor-in-Chief John Patrick Mateo earned the 2nd Most Outstanding Campus Journalist award.
Opinion-Editorial Editor Stephanie Estrella’s piece, “Pundido ang ilaw sa susunod na kalsada”, made her the 4th Most Outstanding Editorial Writer and Punto Central Luzon’s Choice for Most Outstanding Editorial Writer.
Meanwhile, Head of Visual Arts Maryisobelle Arcilla was named the 10th Most Outstanding Editorial Cartoonist in another Luzon-wide stint.
The annual awards, featuring 46 publications from various regions in the north, saw The Forefront emerge as one of Luzon’s best.

# CHTM Sharks Roar at 2nd CHTM Rally 2025
[Image: CHTM Sharks Roar at 2nd CHTM Rally 2025]
[CHTM](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/chtm/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Thursday, September 11, 2025**
GORDON COLLEGE — The College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) filled the East Tapinac Covered Court with cheers and chants as the 2nd CHTM Rally unfolded last September 9, 2025, igniting the spirit of the CHTM Sharks in preparation for the much-anticipated Siklab 2025 Sportsfest on September 15–19, 2025.
The event showcased the final lineup of the College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) official teams and players.
Furthermore, athletes from the CHTM Sharks introduced themselves through lively intermission numbers performed by each sports team, adding excitement and entertainment to the rally.
Player representatives from each team also participated in a brief interview with the Masters of Ceremony, where they shared their thoughts and enthusiasm for the upcoming Siklab competition.
Moreover, the event was organized in collaboration with the College of Hospitality and Tourism Management Student Council (CHTM-SC), Arapaap Productions, the Junior Association of Hospitality Management Students (JAHMS), and the League of Tourism Students of the Philippines (LTSP), who worked together to ensure the program’s success.
The College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) Dean, Dr. Mark Alvin Lazaro, Assistant Dean Vincent Dela Cruz, Bachelor of Science and Tourism Management (BSTM) Program Coordinator Ma’am Lizette Ann P. Sia, Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management (BSHM) Coordinator Vince Richard Gomez, and ARAPAAP Adviser Ms. Jenny Mae M. Lagman also extended strong support and leadership, which greatly guided the preparations for the rally.
To cap off the event, the atmosphere reached its peak as the CHTM Sharks filled the covered court with their department’s official Siklab cheer, embodying their spirit of unity and readiness for the upcoming sportsfest.| via Lovely Doroin/The FOREFRONT

# 𝟗 𝐆𝐂𝐈𝐀𝐍𝐒 𝐏𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐄𝐃 𝐂𝐏𝐀𝐋𝐄 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓; 𝐆𝐂 𝐑𝐄𝐂𝐎𝐑𝐃𝐒 𝟓𝟔.𝟐𝟓% 𝐏𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐑𝐀𝐓𝐄
[Image: 𝟗 𝐆𝐂𝐈𝐀𝐍𝐒 𝐏𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐄𝐃 𝐂𝐏𝐀𝐋𝐄 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓; 𝐆𝐂 𝐑𝐄𝐂𝐎𝐑𝐃𝐒 𝟓𝟔.𝟐𝟓% 𝐏𝐀𝐒𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐑𝐀𝐓𝐄]
[CBA](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/cba/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, June 7, 2025**
Gordon College (GC) College of Business and Accountrancy (CBA) records 9 new Certified Public Accountant (CPA) in the recently held May 2025 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Exam (CPALE).
The institution aimed an overall perfomance of 56.25%, which surpassed the national rating of 33.11%, with a total of 9 out of 16 examinees joining 3,156 new CPAs in the country.
Out of 13 first time examinees, 8 passed the examination, with 2 considered as conditional. Additionally, among the 3 repeaters, 1 passed while another 1 was classified as conditional.
The licensure examination was administered by the Professional Regulation Comission (PRC) from May 25 to 27 nationwide.
Source: Professional Regulation Commission (PRC)

# GC Records 3,127 Freshmen for New Academic Year
[Image: GC Records 3,127 Freshmen for New Academic Year]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, October 18, 2025**
GORDON COLLEGE MAIN CAMPUS —Gordon College (GC) experiences an increase in its total student population for Academic Year 2025–2026, highlighted by a significant surge in freshmen enrollment across all college departments.
According to the official report from the Office of the College Registrar, the total student population rose from 8,625 this Academic Year (A.Y.) 2025-2026, in contrast to the 7,505 recorded Gcians last 2024–2025.
Furthermore, the number of Level 1 students also recorded a drastic jump from 2,731 to 3,127 freshmen.
The College of Business and Accountancy (CBA) continues to lead as the largest department, with 2,431 total students and 767 freshmen for this academic year.
The College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS) recorded a population of 1,642 students and 676 freshmen.
The College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) also experienced a notable increase in freshmen enrollees, from 468 last year to 663 this year.
While the College of Allied Health Studies (CAHS) saw an increase from 422 to 500 freshmen.
The College of Computer Studies (CCS) also recorded additional enrollees, welcoming 521 freshmen this year compared to the previous 442 record.
In line with its continuous growth, the CBA has officially moved into its new home at the GC Annex Building in Kalaklan, marking a new chapter for the college. | via Frances Marie Farne/The FOREFRONT

# Online Application for GC Admission Test Procedure (1st Semester, A.Y. 2024-2025)
[Image: Online Application for GC Admission Test Procedure (1st Semester, A.Y. 2024-2025)]
[OSWS](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/osws/)
**Monday, December 18, 2023**
**[Image: 🟢]
STEP 1. CREATE ONLINE PORTAL ACCOUNT**
1.1 Go to Gordon College Admission Portal login page (<https://gordoncollegeccs.edu.ph/gca>)
1.2 Click “Create Account”
1.3 Type your email address, given name, last name, date of birth, contact number, desired password and select type of student (New Student, Transferee, Second Courser)
1.4 Click “Register”
Notes:
o A valid and existing email address is required in this process.
o Do not create multiple accounts as this will be a ground for disapproval of application.
· Do not forget your email and password
**[Image: 🟢]
STEP 2. LOG ON TO YOUR ACCOUNT**
2.1 Go to the portal login page
2.2 Type your previously registered email address and password then click “Log In”
2.3 You will be directed to the portal Dashboard.
2.4 The Dashboard displays the status of your application.
[Image: 🟢]
 **STEP 3. PROFILING**
3.1 On the upper left side of the page, click “Upload Photo” to upload your recent photo.
Guide:
o 2×2 colored picture, white background
o Formal pose wearing collared top, No eyeglasses or any accessories like earrings.
o Picture should be taken not later than one week prior to filing of application.
3.2 On the Menu, click “Profile”
3.3 Completely and accurately fill out the forms (Personal Information, Family Background and Desired Programs)
3.4 Read the Gordon College General Data Privacy Notice and click the CHECKBOX.
3.5 Review the form and click “Submit”
**[Image: 🟢]
STEP 4. UPLOADING OF DOCUMENTS**
4.1 On the Menu, click “Uploads”
4.2 Upload scanned or clear image of the required documents. Click the placeholder to browse for an image to upload.
4.3 The image file should be less than 2MB to avoid uploading errors
Required documents:
o Recent Good Moral Character Certificate
o PSA Authenticated Birth Certificate
o Senior High School ID or Any Valid ID Card
– Click “Submit” to finalize the uploading.
[Image: 🟢]
 **STEP 5. GCAT Schedule**
5.1 The schedule of GCAT will be posted to your portal account within three (3) working days after submission of COMPLETE application and required documents.
5.2 Upon posting of the test schedule on the online portal, you may download and print the following:
o GCAT Schedule slip
o Student Information Sheet
————————————————–
What to bring on the test day?
1. GCAT Schedule Slip
2. Student Information Sheets
3. Senior High School or any valid ID Card
5. Pencil and Pen
Note: Please be informed that all applications shall be submitted online to prevent the spread of Covid-19.


### Source: https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/paulino-welcomes-9k-studes-with-new-building-rates-gc-as-highly-university-ready

# Paulino welcomes 9k studes with new building; rates GC as highly university-ready
[Image: Paulino welcomes 9k studes with new building; rates GC as highly university-ready]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, October 18, 2025**
GORDON COLLEGE MAIN CAMPUS — Coinciding with PAGLALAYAG 2025 (more commonly known as Apertura 2025), the newly acquired Gordon College Annex Building, located at Lower Kalaklan, Olongapo, was formally inaugurated on August 11.
In an interview with The Forefront, Olongapo City Mayor Atty. Rolen C. Paulino Jr. “wanted to be practical” in expanding Gordon College (GC), citing several important considerations.
Paulino believes that students applied to Gordon College for quality education, a main reason to attract 9,500 students this Academic Year (A.Y).
As the A.Y. 2025-2026 begins, the local chief executive highlighted their desire to make ongoing improvements to the current building and structure, ensuring new equipment is added as needed.
“We want to make sure that everything goes accordingly. Gusto talaga naming mag-expand,” the mayor said.
The back-to-back mayor of Olongapo City also considered improving and adding programs that would need more equipment and facilities.
“Tinitingnan din natin ‘yong possibility na mag-expand pa tayo kasi may clamor din to add additional [programs], whether more medical courses or engineering, lahat ‘yan pinag-iisipan namin,” the mayor added.
Now, the College of Business and Accountancy (CBA) has officially moved to the newly inaugurated annex building of the institution.
When asked about the institution’s readiness for university status, the Board of Trustees Chairperson gave the institution a rating of 8 to 9 out of 10, stressing that while “the qualifications [are] there and personnel [are] there”, there remains the challenge of “accumulating enough resources to qualify.”
Moreover, the chairperson spoke of the institution being already at that point as “the quality of education [that Gordon College] provides is at par with some of the universities.”
“Sa results ng [board] exams natin, we’re always competing with the best universities,” he added.
Furthermore, the mayor underscored the need to instill professionalism and discipline among students through the institution, aiming to make them employable and ready to become future managers. He also nurtured and wished for the students to apply values of professionalism and intelligence to work hand-in-hand when enrolled within the institution.
“[Please] know that the city government is here to support the institution and the students. The city is always proud of Gordon College. It’s the home of many top-notchers, many successful community leaders, both in business and society. Mataas ang accreditation natin, we are internationally ranked, [and] we are very proud of the school and very proud of its students,” he concluded. | via Keane Rafael Abdon/The FOREFRONT

# GC Color Run Kicks Off 27th Founding Anniversary
[Image: GC Color Run Kicks Off 27th Founding Anniversary]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, February 22, 2026**
The annual GC FUNdation RUN marked the start of Gordon College’s 27th Founding Anniversary, held on February 22, 2026, at the East Tapinac Oval Track.
The event gathered members of the Gordon College Faculty Association (GCFAS), administrative staff, students, alumni, and community participants under the pre-foundation day celebration motif, “Color Run.”
The program commenced with the assembly of participants, followed by an opening ceremony that featured welcome messages from Dr. Katherine Yap and Dr. Imelda D.P. Soriano. A Zumba warm-up session, led by administrators, faculty members, and students from the Bachelor of Physical Education (BPED), energized attendees ahead of the race.
The run officially started at 6:30 AM as participants filled the track dressed in white shirts and athletic attire, ready to be splashed with vibrant colored powder and water.
More than a display of color and movement, this year’s FUNdation RUN is a colorful display of the institution’s commitment to promoting wellness, unity, and community relations while marking the upcoming foundation celebration with lively and memorable moments. | via Sam Andrea R. Delos Reyes/The FOREFRONT

# Cosme Y. Sering Library is Now Open
[Image: Cosme Y. Sering Library is Now Open]
[LIMC](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/limc/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, January 18, 2025**
Today marks a significant milestone for Gordon College, as we celebrate the blessing of the newly renovated Cosme Y. Sering Library. Made possible through the generous donation of the Acevedo Family, this library serves as a vital resource for students, faculty, and the Olongapo City community, promoting learning, collaboration, and access to knowledge.
The Acevedo Family’s generosity exemplifies their commitment to education and community development. This improved facility enhances academic opportunities and enriches the educational experience for students and stakeholders alike.
We extend our deepest gratitude to the Acevedo Family, Hon. Rolen C. Paulino, Former City Mayor, Hon. Rolen C. Paulino Jr., Olongapo City Mayor, Hon/ Cristabelle Marie “Tata” Paulino, Committee on Education Chairperson, Hon. Sarah Lugerna Lipumano-Garcia, City Councilor, Hon. Benjamin G. Cajudo II, Former City Councilor, Dr. Lora Yusi, CHEDROIII Director, Dr. Imelda DP. Soriano, OIC-College President, the City Officials, Board of Trustees, College Officials, College Personnel, Student Leaders, and everyone who contributed to this meaningful endeavor.
With its legacy of excellence and commitment to progress, Gordon College remains steadfast in providing quality education and opportunities for its students and the community. Together, we celebrate the transformative power of education and its enduring impact on society.

# ONLINE Adding/Dropping of Classes
[Image: ONLINE Adding/Dropping of Classes]
**Monday, January 19, 2026**
**ANNOUNCEMENT:**
**ONLINE Adding/Dropping of Classes**
*Second Semester Academic Year 2025-2026*
**January 19-30, 2026**
[Image: ☑️]
Step 1
Log-on to the student portal ([https://gordoncollegeccs.edu.ph/gces/student](https://gordoncollegeccs.edu.ph/gces/student?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAYnJpZBExZWpzSlY3MHlQdVJWaXA0bnNydGMGYXBwX2lkEDIyMjAzOTE3ODgyMDA4OTIAAR5DCtJJZeE0IeMkAlOWYkAjlJ5HTa_uyuxL5M64lTq3dzJieHkPXJaQ0YalBg_aem_XfOZPmWrrx4p7jcYpDLqDg))
Click Add/Drop Request Button under Menu Items.
[Image: ☑️]
Step 2
To request for Dropping of classes, under Current Schedule section, click Drop button.
To request for adding of classes, under Add Subjects section, type the detail of the class (you can search by class code, subject or by description) on the search box. Click Add button of the desired class.
[Image: ☑️]
Step 3
Your selected subject(s) will appear under List of Subjects to Add/Drop section. Repeat step 2 to add or drop more classes.
Click submit to finalize your request or cancel to clear selected classes.
[Image: ☑️]
Step 4
Your request will be evaluated by your program coordinator and will be verified by the college registrar.
Regularly visit the GCES portal for request updates.

# LCUAA 2025 Welcomes Rainy Sunday Afternoon
[Image: LCUAA 2025 Welcomes Rainy Sunday Afternoon]
[LCUAA](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/lcuaa/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, October 19, 2025**
The eagerly anticipated week-long 14th LCUAA National Games officially kicked off today at the City of San Jose del Monte (CSJDM) Sports Complex.
Cheers and applause filled the venue as the opening ceremony began with a parade featuring all 27 participating colleges, each led by their institution’s gold medalists.
Following the parade was the introduction of the LCUAA 2025 representative officers, a doxology by the Sining Tanglawan ng San Jose del Monte Performing Group, the singing of the National Anthem and the San Jose del Monte city hymn, and an energetic dance performance by the San Joseño World Class Talents troupe.
City College of San Jose del Monte (CCSJDM) College President Dr. Roger S. Ambida delivered the opening remarks, warmly welcoming delegates to the institution.
Hon. Arturo B. Robes then gave the keynote address, encouraging athletes to build a brighter and more empowered future.
Additionally, Dr. Lora L. Yusi, CHED Region 3 Director IV, gave an inspiring speech, highlighting the significance of LCUAA 2025 as a testament to the growth of local universities: “We see scholars who dream larger than themselves.”
The competitive events officially begin tomorrow, October 20, 2025.
Stay tuned to the official Facebook page of The Forefront for updates on the 14th LCUAA National Games. | via Alyssa Marie Alcantara / The FOREFRONT

FRONTLINES | 𝑰𝒏 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒕𝒐 𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒌 𝒘𝒊𝒔𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒗𝒐𝒕𝒆 𝒔𝒎𝒂𝒓𝒕, 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒚𝒐𝒏𝒆 𝒓𝒆𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒚 𝒔𝒂𝒚, ‘𝑰 𝒕𝒉𝒐𝒖𝒈𝒉𝒕 𝒘𝒊𝒔𝒆𝒍𝒚 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒗𝒐𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒔𝒎𝒂𝒓𝒕’?

# Fostering Mental Health
[Image: Fostering Mental Health]
[Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/extension/) [RDCES](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/rdces/) [Community Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/community-extension/)
**Wednesday, July 26, 2023**
In adherence to our commitment to community service, the GC Community Extension Services Unit (GC-CESU), in collaboration with the GC Guidance Office and Tapinac Senior High School, successfully organized and conducted a seminar on July 31, 2023. The seminar aimed to enhance the resilience of the attendees by equipping them with techniques to address and manage challenges, emphasizing the importance of self-care, addressing mental health stigma, and facilitating access to mental health services. Ms. Mechel Bautista, GC Guidance Office Head, served as the resource speaker. The seminar saw active participation from 42 teachers from Tapinac Senior High School and took place at the Gordon College function hall.

# BLEPT 2025 Yields 200 New GC-Produced Professional Teachers
[Image: BLEPT 2025 Yields 200 New GC-Produced Professional Teachers]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Monday, December 22, 2025**
The College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS) beams with pride as it yields 39 Licensed Professional Teachers (LPTs) for the Elementary level and 161 new LPTs for the Secondary level at this year’s Board Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers (BLEPT)
Gordon College (GC) once again surpassed the national passing rates in the Board Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers (BLEPT) conducted on September 21 and November 30, 2025.
For the Elementary Level, 39 out of 49 Gordon College examinees passed the LEPT, resulting in a passing rate of 79.59% against a national passing rate of 51.04%.
Meanwhile, for the Secondary Level, 161 out of 177 Gordon College examinees passed the LEPT, posting an overall passing rate of 90.96%, with 50% of second-takers also passing.
Overall, 76,696 out of 122,528 examinees nationwide passed the September–November 2025 BLEPT, representing a national passing rate of 65.04% for the secondary level.
Notably, the Board Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers (BLEPT) was rescheduled in Regions I, II and Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) due to inclement weather.
The examinations for the said regions were conducted on November 30. | via Lovely Doroin/The FOREFRONT

# GC Library Renovation: 40% Done
[Image: GC Library Renovation: 40% Done]
[LIMC](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/limc/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Monday, August 19, 2024**
The Gordon College library is currently undergoing renovation project which aims at transforming the space into a more dynamic and student-friendly environment.
In an interview with The Forefront, Mr. Marlon Atencio, the college librarian, provided detailed updates and valuable insights into the objectives, current developments, and anticipated benefits of the project for students and faculty alike.
According to Mr. Atencio, the upgraded library is shifting towards a “learning commons” setup.
“Kasi yung college library natin ang mangyayari ay parang learning commons na siya, kumbaga parang café setup,” he shared.
In addition, the college librarian announced plans to enhance the library by installing vending machines, similar to those at ground floor, allowing students to enjoy snacks—though only solid foods, other snacks, will be permitted, with liquids excluded.
He further mentioned that the timeline for the renovation’s completion remains flexible.
“Wala naman binigay na timeline, ang gusto lang manyari is as soon as possible matapos siya para siyempre magamit na ito ng mga estudyante.” he added
As of now, the renovation is around 40% complete. Key areas such as the computer section and audiovisual room are being redesigned with high-quality materials.
Moreover, he also shared that various areas, such as the flooring are already underway and the renovation is focusing on upgrading both the structural and aesthetic aspects of the library to ensure a premium experience for GCians.
Students and faculty can look forward to an enhanced library experience. The space are expected to be more conducive to learning with upgraded seating, including sofas and modern furniture.
Furthermore, the college librarian also mentioned that they should not only expect the library to be well-maintained but also that its services will be improved to ensure that students can use it effectively.
In addressing the specific needs of students and faculty, the library will host separate orientation sessions to familiarize students with the new setup.
“Kaya hindi kami nakisabay sa student orientation kasi magkakaroon kami ng separate orientation sa library, wherein ang gagawin namin ay mag-kakaroon ng library tour ang bawat section, para alam nila kung paano gamitin lahat ng area, para maiwasan din natin [na] nahihirapan kung paano i-access [ang] mga gamit, pati mga electronics resources lahat ‘yon it-tackle natin during orientation,” he explains.
Next, he also discussed changes in the physical layout, such as new glass doors and relocating the lockers outside the library.
Additionally, he encouraged students to reach out through the library’s Facebook page for online inquiries.
Once completed, the renovated Gordon College library promises to be a welcoming and efficient learning space for all that fosters both learning and collaboration.

# Avoid Cellphone Use on Stairs
[Image: Avoid Cellphone Use on Stairs]
**Friday, April 17, 2026**
**Safety Reminder Regarding Cellphone Use on Stairways**  
To ensure the safety of all students and faculty, we are reminding everyone of the following guideline regarding electronic device usage on stairs:
**Policy:**  
Cellphone use is strictly prohibited while ascending or descending staircases. This includes texting, browsing social media, making calls, or playing games.
**Rationale:**  
Stairways are high-traffic areas that require full attention. Using a cellphone while walking significantly reduces spatial awareness and reaction time, increasing the risk of:
* Slips, trips and falls
* Collisions with other students
* Blocking the flow of traffic during passing periods
**Procedure:**
* **Pause:** If you must send a message or answer a call, step to the side and stop walking before using your device.
* **Pocket:** Keep phones stored in pockets or bags while navigating steps.
* **Proceed:** Only resume walking once the device is put away and your full attention is on the stairs.
Thank you for helping us keep our campus safe.


### Source: https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/rights-of-the-data-subjects

# Rights of the Data Subjects
The stakeholders are the primary data subjects of Gordon College. They are the students, their parents or guardians, the employees (regardless of their employment status), officials, visitors, donors/ sponsors, service providers, and the like are entitled to the following rights with regards to their personal data:
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-informed-01]
## Rights to be Informed
* The data subject has a right to be informed whether personal data pertaining to him or her shall be, are being, or have been processed, including the existence of automated decision-making and profiling.
* The data subject shall be notified and furnished with information indicated hereunder before the entry of his or her personal data into the processing system of Gordon College, or at the next practical opportunity:
  + Description of the personal data to be entered into the system;
  + Purposes for which they are being or will be processed, including processing for direct marketing, profiling or historical, statistical or scientific purpose;
  + Basis of processing, when processing is not based on the consent of the data subject;
  + Scope and method of the personal data processing;
  + Third-party recipients or classes of recipients to whom the personal data are or may be disclosed;
  + Methods utilized for automated access, if the same is allowed by the data subject, and the extent to which such access is authorized, including meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject;
  + The identity and contact details of Gordon College or its representative;
  + The period for which the information will be stored; and
  + The existence of their rights as data subjects, including the right to access, correction, and object to the processing, as well as the right to lodge a complaint before the National Privacy Commission.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/the-right-to-be-informed/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_object-02]
## Right to Object
The data subject shall have the right to object to the processing of his or her personal data, including processing for direct marketing, automated processing or profiling. The data subject shall also be notified and given an opportunity to withhold consent to the processing in case of changes or any amendment to the information supplied or declared to the data subject in the preceding paragraph.  
When a data subject objects or withholds consent, Gordon College may not be able to conduct academic, administrative and other functions or services related to the data subject.  
When a data subject objects or withholds consent, Gordon College shall no longer process the personal data, unless:
* The personal data is needed pursuant to a subpoena;
* The collection and processing are for obvious purposes, including, when it is necessary for the performance of or in relation to a contract or service to which the data subject is a party, or when necessary or desirable in the context of an employer-employee relationship between the collector and the data subject;
* The information is being collected and processed as a result of a legal obligation; or
* Gordon College’s functions as the local college or as an instrumentality of the government will be impaired.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-object/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-access-03]
## Right to Access
The data subject has the right to reasonable access to, upon demand providing sufficient time for preparation, the following:
* Contents of his or her personal data that were processed;
* Sources from which personal data were obtained;
* Names and addresses of recipients of the personal data;
* Manner by which such data were processed;
* Reasons for the disclosure of the personal data to recipients, if any;
* Information on automated processes where the data will, or is likely to, be made as the sole basis for any decision that significantly affects or will affect the data subject;
  + Date when his or her personal data concerning the data subject were last accessed and modified; and
  + The description of Gordon College under Olongapo City Ordinance 07 Series of 2018.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-access/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-correct-04]
## Right to Correct/ Rectification
The data subject has the right to dispute the inaccuracy or error in the personal data and have Gordon College correct it within a reasonable period and accordingly, unless the request is vexatious or otherwise unreasonable. If the personal data has been corrected, Gordon College shall ensure the accessibility of both the new and the retracted information and the simultaneous receipt of the new and the retracted information by the intended recipients thereof: provided, that recipients or third parties who have previously received such processed personal data shall be informed of its inaccuracy and its rectification, upon reasonable request of the Data Subject.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-rectify/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-eraser-05]
## Right to Block/ Remove/ Erasure/ Be Forgotten
These rights of erasure and blocking do not apply to personal data, documents, records and accounts which are part of Gordon College public records as an instrumentality of the government or as the local college.
The data subject shall have the right to suspend, withdraw or order the blocking, removal or destruction of his or her personal data from Gordon College’s filing system.
* This right may be exercised upon discovery and substantial proof of any of the following:
  + The personal data is incomplete, outdated, false, or unlawfully obtained;
  + The personal data is being used for purpose not authorized by the  
    data subject;
  + The personal data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which  
    they were collected;
  + The data subject withdraws consent or objects to the processing, and there is no other legal ground or overriding legitimate interest for the processing;
  + The processing is unlawful;
  + Gordon College personal information processor violated the rights of the data subject.
* Gordon College may notify third parties who have previously received such  
  processed personal data.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-erasure-or-blocking/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-complaint-06]
## Right to File a Complaint
You have the right to lodge a complaint if you are the subject of a data privacy violation.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-file-a-complaint/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-damages-09]
## Right to be Indemnified/ to Damages
This right to damages is subordinate to:
* The presumption of Gordon College regularity in the performance of government functions;
* As applicable, the principle that the State may not be sued without its consent; and
* The non-liability of Gordon College arising from the incidental damages due to Gordon College’s pursuance of its mandates or compliance with its legal obligations.
The data subject shall be indemnified for any damages sustained due to such inaccurate, incomplete, outdated, false, unlawfully obtained or unauthorized use of personal data, taking into account any violation of his or her rights and freedoms as data subject.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-damages/>
[Image: 300px\_300px\_rights-portability-08]
## Right to Portability
As a data subject, you have the right to obtain from the PIC a copy of your personal data and/or have the same transmitted from one PIC to another, in an electronic or structured format that is commonly used.
For more information you may refer to <https://privacy.gov.ph/right-to-data-portability/>

# CEAS Women’s Historic Smash Hit: Another Gold in Futsal Match
[Image: CEAS Women’s Historic Smash Hit: Another Gold in Futsal Match]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, September 19, 2025**
What a thrilling clash between pink and blue.
The College of Education, Arts and Sciences (CEAS) Mentors defeated College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) Sharks after a long showdown that ended in 3-0, and finished as champions in the Women’s Futsal match on the last day of SIKLAB 2025, held at New Asinan covered court.
The Mentors did not let their guard down ever since their first game, making sure everything is coordinated to one another until the final match.
Cheers roared through the court as the intensifying moments of the game went on, with Mentors maintaining their momentum throughout the match.

# TF SECURES LHEPC SPOT
[Image: TF SECURES LHEPC SPOT]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, February 14, 2026**
The Forefront journos once again demonstrated their grit and skills in campus journalism, securing several awards at the 24th Regional Higher Education Press Conference (RHEPC), held at Palm Cabanas Resort, Arayat, Pampanga, from February 11 to 13.
Two of the publication’s outgoing executive members, John Patrick Mateo (Editor-in-Chief) and Lance Isaac Leon (Associate Editor), were recognized as Outstanding Tertiary Campus Journalists (OTCJ) in Region III.
In the group category, the pub’s entry for Opening Billboard ranked 4th Place overall.
In individual categories, delegates from the publication bagged nine (9) awards as listed below.
Angelique Jose
1st Place – Traditional Literary Graphics Illustration (English)
Lance Isaac Leon
2nd Place – Editorial Writing (English)
3rd Place – Opinion Writing (English)
John Patrick Mateo
3rd Place – Devcom Writing (Filipino)
John Christian Rocero
3rd Place – Photojournalism (English)
Mary Isobelle Arcilla
5th Place – Traditional Comic Strip Drawing (English)
6th Place – Traditional Editorial Cartooning (English)
Keane Rafael Abdon
8th Place – News Writing (English)
Mikhaela Sagun
10th Place – Poetry Writing (English)
Overall, The Forefront is the 11th Highest Pointer in individual categories against 42 participating college publications in Central Luzon.
Additionally, Keane Rafael Abdon is the newly elected division coordinator of Olongapo City for the Young Journalist Association of Region III (YJAR-III).
Five campus journalists from the publication, who garnered top 5 placements in their respective categories, will advance to the 21st Luzon-Wide Higher Education Press Conference (LHEPC) in Tuguegarao City, Cagayan, next month to compete in eight categories. | via Mikhaela Sagun and Lance Isaac Leon, THE FOREFRONT

# Gordon College Joins the 2025 Times Higher Education Impact Rankings
[Image: Gordon College Joins the 2025 Times Higher Education Impact Rankings]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, June 18, 2025**
We are proud to announce that Gordon College has officially earned a place in the prestigious Times Higher Education (THE) Impact Rankings 2025! Despite being a newcomer to the global stage, GC was ranked among the top 1,500+ out of 2,526 higher education institutions (HEIs) from 130 countries, assessed for their contributions to achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs)—a recognition based on universities’ social impact through research, stewardship, outreach, and teaching.
Gordon College participated in four SDG categories and earned the following standings:
• SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being: Ranked 1001–1500
• SDG 4 – Quality Education: Ranked 1501+
• SDG 10 – Reduced Inequalities: Ranked 1001+
• SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals: Ranked 1501+
More than just recognition, this milestone reflects our evolving vision—to become a globally recognized local institution making meaningful contributions to global progress through inclusive, equitable, and sustainable development in higher education.

# Final presentation of Project METRO
[Image: Final presentation of Project METRO]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, April 17, 2026**
April 16, 2026 | Final presentation of Project METRO: Monitoring Enforcement Tracking Resource Online with DTI Zambales and Gordon College – College of Computer Studies.
Present during the final presentation are DTI3 CPD Acting Division Chief Jose Antonio Toledo, DTI Zambales CPD Division Chief Neil John M. Fabay, Gordon College CCS Dean Ronnie D. Luy, Gordon College CCS Asst Dean Armilyn T. Martinez, and Gordon College CCS Prof. Reynaldo G. Bautista. The panelist provided expert guidance and valuable insights to further refining the system.
Project METRO is intended to make market inspections and fair trade monitoring more efficient, transparent, and fully digitized. In practical terms, the system aims to help government personnel carry out inspections more systematically while improving documentation, reporting, and coordination in the field.
The use of a digital platform for inspections will also help strengthen public trust by making enforcement more transparent and easier to document. In many cases, digitized systems can support more consistent monitoring while reducing gaps in manual processes.

# LPCC IKOT PALENGKE PROJECT METRO: Monitorning Enforcement and Tracking Resource Outline
[Image: LPCC IKOT PALENGKE PROJECT METRO: Monitorning Enforcement and Tracking Resource Outline]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Thursday, January 15, 2026**
January 15, 2026 | DTI Zambales initial coordination meeting with Gordon College for the development of LPCC Ikot Palengke PROJECT METRO: Monitoring Enforcement & Tracking Resource Online.
The LPCC Ikot Palengke Project METRO: Monitoring Enforcement & Tracking Resource Online is a digital system intended to support government operations in consumer protection, price monitoring, fair trade enforcement, and public service delivery. The project aims to modernize data collection, reporting, monitoring, and analytics through the use of information systems and emerging technologies.

# “2,000 change-makers” attend NSTP grad ‘25
[Image: “2,000 change-makers” attend NSTP grad ‘25]
[NSTP](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/nstp/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, June 8, 2025**
Two thousand Gordon College (GC) students enrolled in their National Service and Training Program (NSTP) courses filled the SMX Convention Center, Olongapo City, on Wednesday, for this year’s NSTP Graduation Ceremony.
With the theme, “Volunteerism in Action: Shaping Leaders, Strengthening Community”, this year’s batch of NSTP graduates was graced by Miss Manila 2014 Dr. Krischelle D. Halili.
Dr. Halili emphasized that leadership is an “act not for yourself, but for others” in her address. “Serve something greater than yourself and take your friends with you.”
Moreover, she called on students to love the country and God while also channeling ‘tech natives’ to participate in online community initiatives as well as community services and university council activities on-site.
Leading the initial confirmation of the graduates, Vice President for Academic Affairs Dr. Darwin P. Paguio also delivered his special message, focusing on the impact of genuine leadership.
“True leadership is not defined merely by title or accolades but by the impact you make in the lives of others,” he said as he congratulated the “two thousand change-makers” afterward.
This was followed by the awarding of certificates to Literary Training Service (LTS) and Civic Welfare Training Service (CWTS) completers from the different departments of the institution.
NSTP Instructor Mr. Hubert Lew Magrata delivered his closing remarks to officially close the program.

# CHTM reps shine at 18th Philippine Food Expo 2026; Faculty-student tandem secure bronze
[Image: CHTM reps shine at 18th Philippine Food Expo 2026; Faculty-student tandem secure bronze]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, April 24, 2026**
Students and faculty from the Gordon College – College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (GC-CHTM) showcased their skills and creativity at the 18th Philippine Food Expo 2026, held from April 17 to 19 at the World Trade Center Manila.
Leading GC-CHTM’s performance, Mr. Michael Dela Cruz, a CHTM faculty member, and Christian Jhay Quioc, a 4th-year BSHM student, secured a bronze medal in the PINASarap Breakfast Competition with their expertly crafted breakfast meal.
Meanwhile, Mr. Vince Richard Gomez, a faculty member, together with Mharvie Ann Pastor, a 4th year Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management (BSHM) student, demonstrated culinary skills in the Creative Filipino Dessert Platter Competition.
In the Philippine Food Expo Knowledge Challenge, Sharmaine Claire Baldo, a 4th year Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management (BSTM) student, and Heidi Lyne Bajado, a 4th-year BSHM student, showcased strong knowledge and coordination throughout the competition.
Meanwhile, Nikki Vince Neil Yoro, a CHTM faculty member, alongside Reynald Manalo, a 3rd year BSHM student, took part in the Mystery Ingredient Competition, highlighting their creativity and ability to perform under pressure.

# Responsibilities of the Data Subjects
Associated to the exercise of rights are responsibilities to respect the privacy of others and comply with Gordon College’s regulations in its administration of data privacy.
Data subjects shall have the following responsibilities:
1. Respect the data privacy rights of others;
2. Report any suspected security incident or personal data breach to Gordon College Data Protection Officer by sending an email or accomplishing OCP-DPU Form No. 4;
3. Provide Gordon College with true and accurate personal data and other information. Before submitting personal data of different people to Gordon College, obtain the consent of such people.
4. Not disclose to any unauthorized party any non-public confidential, sensitive or personal information obtained or learned in confidence from Gordon College; and
5. Abide by the policies, guidelines and rules of Gordon College on data privacy, information security, records management, research and ethical conduct. From time to time, check for and comply with updates on these policies, guidelines and rules. Students may also refer to their Student Handbook.

# Gordon College Faculty Join Basic FSL Training to Promote Inclusive Education
[Image: Gordon College Faculty Join Basic FSL Training to Promote Inclusive Education]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, August 29, 2025**
Faculty members from the College of Education, Arts and Sciences (CEAS) and the College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) with Mr. Joseph Atencio-OIC, Head of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Unit proudly took part in a three-day Basic Filipino Sign Language (FSL) Training held last August 26–28, 2025 at the SMX Convention Center, Olongapo City. The event was organized by the Olongapo City Persons with Disability Affairs Office (PDAO) in collaboration with the Department of Education – Olongapo City Division Office.
Throughout the training, participants engaged in interactive and hands-on activities designed to equip educators with the skills to communicate effectively with the Deaf—nurturing a more inclusive, and compassionate learning environment.
This initiative not only strengthened our instructors’ professional competencies but also reaffirmed their dedication to accessibility, diversity, and inclusivity in education—a true reflection of Gordon College’s commitment to ensuring that no learner is left behind.
