Duty- and tax-free privileges are granted to certain people. Section 800 of
the CMTA provides duty- and tax-free privileges to returning Filipino residents,
who have stayed in a foreign country for a period of at least six months; overseas
Filipino workers (OFWs) who hold valid passports and working in a foreign
country under employment contracts; and overseas Filipinos who now reside or
are citizens of other countries and are coming to resettle in the Philippines.
Balikbayans are also entitled to such privileges. Aside from OFWs and overseas
Filipinos, balikbayans include “Filipino citizens who have been continuously
out of the Philippines for a period of at least one year”.

Filipinos who work and reside in other countries generally fill the
Balikbayan boxes throughout the year and send them to their families a few
months before the Christmas or New Year season, as well as other significant
holidays. The increase begins in September, which marks the beginning of the
Christmas season for many Filipinos. The majority of these balikbayan boxes
arriving at the Port of Manila are from Asian countries, with Canada and the
United States following closely behind (Tristram, 2023).

CONCLUSION
Based on the findings generated from the study, the following conclusions
were hereby drawn:
1. The majority of the respondents were aged 31-40 years old and
primarily were females and working in China (Hong Kong) for
about 0-5 years abroad and from Region III and had sent Balikbayan
Boxes below 10 times.

52 | Pa ge
2. The result exhibited that the respondents were moderately
knowledgeable in terms of their level of knowledge of the guidelines
concerning Republic Act No. 10863 section 800 (g).
3. From the study, it was also concluded that the respondents were
moderately aware in terms of their level of awareness being described
in terms of the contents of Republic Act No. 10863 section 800 (g).
4. Awareness of Overseas Filipino Workers in terms of age was
found to be significant. Similarly, knowledge of OFWs in terms of country
of work, the region in the Philippines, and the number of times sent a
Balikbayan Box was also found to be significant. The rest of the
variables affirm the null hypothesis that there is no significant
difference between the knowledge and awareness of the respondents
when grouped according to profile variables.
5. To help develop and improve the knowledge and awareness of the
OFWs of the various guidelines about Republic Act No. 10863, section
800 (g) Balikbayan Boxes, an infographic is made containing essential
information about how to send a balikbayan box, the requirements
needed, the restricted and prohibited goods, and the privilege that
OFWs may avail in sending balikbayan boxes. Furthermore, aside
from an infographic, a plan of action is hereby proposed to
disseminate both knowledge & awareness regarding Republic Act No.
10863, 800 (g). The specific activity is to disseminate essential tools that
will help respondents become more knowledgeable and aware by
intensifying social media use through posting in OFW social media
groups and sending messages via Messenger, Viber, or any social
media platforms available.
RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on the findings and conclusions of the following
recommendations are provided to enhance the Knowledge and Awareness of
the guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863 balikbayan boxes of
Overseas Filipino Workers.
1. Full coordination among the Shipping Companies and Overseas
Filipino Workers and the Bureau of Customs engaging in the
transaction may be watched to ensure the operation's efficiency.
2. The Bureau of Customs may provide an effective dissemination of
information about the guidelines concerning Republic Act No. 10863
balikbayan box to Overseas Filipino Workers.
3. All Overseas Filipino Workers may have an easy access to a
portal/site that allows them to obtain all of the necessary information when
sending a balikbayan box to their loved ones.
4. The Bureau of Customs may develop adequate communication
with all Overseas Filipino Workers worldwide, expressing their
ideas and feedback for precise quality outcomes.
5. For future researchers to do more exploring regarding the topic to
further enhance the validity and reliability of the study. Also, to explore the
shortcomings and problem of the study to make it more adaptable.

EMPLOYABILITY OF BS CUSTOMS ADMINISTRATION GRADUATES OF GORDON COLLEGE
YEAR 2018-2022
Mary Francine V. Agana, Warren Nikko M. Arenga, Charles Jesper B.
Bantican, Andrie Maurice C. Bacani, Ivan Pineda (+), Ediric D. Gadia, Patricia
Anne Paras.
Gordon College, Olongapo City, Philippines
Abstract: Tracer studies have been employed as a monitoring tool for students'
transition from academic life to professional life. It attempts to follow
graduates' professional progress in relation to the value of the knowledge and
training they received from the college. To determine which courses and
programs have aided the student in achieving the anticipated career path after
graduation, it also provides an assessment of the curriculum design for each of
the relevant courses and programs. This quantitative-descriptive study aimed
to determine the graduates' employability for the Bachelor of Science in
Customs Administration from 2018–2022. This study utilized the descriptive
method of research, in which a total of one hundred four graduates
participated. Data were gathered using the institutional instrument for the
tracer study. Findings revealed that the majority of the graduates secured a job
within a month, with regular status, and are presently employed as
professionals in logistics companies.
Keywords: BSCA graduates, employability, school-related factors, tracer
study.

56 | Pa ge
1. INTRODUCTION
Nowadays, graduates are faced with a challenge of seeking for employment
after graduation. Refozar & Del Mundo (2013) emphasized on their study that
there seem to have a wide gap between number of graduates and absorption
rates. And the usual cause, as claimed, is the apparent weak preparation of
graduates with job requirements of the government and private organizations.
The truth of the matter is that jobs are available, but it seems that very few
qualify for the available jobs. One of the problems of students in getting
employed after graduation is meeting the job requirements that an organization
requires of applicants for a job. However, job requirements vary from company
to company for it has its own set of criteria in human resource procurement and
development. It is therefore the concern of every higher education institution to
provide its students with pre-employment preparations to getting jobs. Such
preparations must be research-based to be sure that the training given to students
would prepare them for employment not only in the provincial or local labor
market, but more importantly, in national and later on in international labor
markets.
The difficulty of finding work after graduation is something that graduates
must overcome. They are searching for the best job opening available. The
intense competition on the labor market and graduates' lack of employability
skills make it difficult for them to find work. According to the Philippine Star
(2017), just one in three college graduates in the nation are "employable," which
indicates that 65 percent of Filipino graduates lack the education and experience
necessary to be qualified for the jobs they are looking for. High unemployment
rates are associated with both economic inefficiency and social instability,
according to Aspiring Minds.
It has been said that the Philippines formal education has been lacking in
producing productive graduates. This goes to say that there is really a need for
students to be trained to become globally competitive, fully equipped with the
proper work values, in order to make a big difference in the world of work. On
their part, they suggested four criteria for evaluating training, such as the reaction
level, the learning level, or how well they learned and retained what they learned,
the behavioral level, and the results level, or the final results obtained from the
training (Refozar and Del Mundo, 2013).
The graduate tracer research offers useful details regarding what happens to
our recent graduates when they enter the workforce. Finding out how well our
institution's training prepares students for their job life as a whole and the extent
to which knowledge, communication, and other abilities have been acquired are
equally essential. The results of this tracer research can also be used as a basis
for future planning activities by offering important data for assessing an
institution's educational and training outcomes (Ramirez et al., 2021).
Numerous studies have examined the employability of graduates from
various courses of graduate track studies based on various research.
Nevertheless, the employability of graduates in customs administration has only
been studied once, and that study focused solely on graduates from a specific
university (Casa et al., 2022). In this study, the researchers intended to find out
the present employment status of Gordon College Bachelor of Science in

57 | Pa ge
Customs Administration graduates. The contribution or benefit of this study is
that it will be one of the bases for the students inside and outside of the school
to inspire them to enroll and continue their college course at Gordon College,
especially if they feel that their path for a career is in customs administration.
Additionally, the researchers, who are enrolled in the same program as the
respondents, believe that this study is important since it will provide
information about the respondents' employability in the future. Finally, this
study will aid future researchers by providing a foundation for their research,
which may eventually relate to the subject or area of interest of this study.
2. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
2.1 Research Design
This study utilizes quantitative research using descriptive method. The
primary goal of the study is to evaluate the employability of BSCA graduates
of Gordon College. The primary goal of the study is to evaluate the
employability of BSCA graduates of Gordon College. Calderon (2006) defined
descriptive research as a purposeful process of gathering, analyzing, classifying,
and tabulating data about prevailing conditions, practices, processes, trends, and
cause-effect relationships and then making adequate and accurate
interpretations about such data with or without or sometimes with minimal aid
of statistical methods. This method is relatively suitable for the study because
it describes the present status of the alumni.
2.2 Research Instrument
The researchers used a survey questionnaire to gather the necessary data
for this study. The questionnaire used is from the Commission on Higher
Education (CHED). The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has
verified the validity and reliability of our survey questionnaire, which has been
in use since its developed by CHED. The questionnaire consists of four main
sections: the respondents' general profile, educational background, post-college
programs, and employment information.
2.3 Treatment of Data
In this study, the data were analyzed and interpreted using the percentage
and frequency distribution methods. This was used to calculate the percentage
distribution and frequency counts of the respondents' personally related
variables. Percentage were used by the researcher to convert the numerical data
gathered from the questionnaire. The descriptive statistic used frequency and
percentage. These things would be explained further in the following:
a. Frequency – pertains to the number of respondents that have the same answer
in a specific question.
b. Percentage – used to determine the ratio of respondents that have the same
answers as the general number of respondents.

CONCLUSION
Based on the findings the following were concluded:
1. The profile of the respondents
Based from the respondents' profiles, the majority are single, most are men, a
substantial number are from region 3, almost all are from Olongapo City, and a
significant proportion live in the city.
10. BASED FROM THE DATA PRESENTED IN THE EMPLOYMENT PROFILE OF THE
RESPONDENTS
The respondents' employment profile indicates that a significant percentage are
employed, with most citing reasons for unemployment as not actively seeking
jobs or lacking job opportunities, the majority holding regular or permanent
positions, a large proportion working as professionals, the vast majority
employed locally, over half securing their first jobs through recommendations,
a substantial portion landing their first jobs in less than a month, and the
majority finding their first jobs relevant to their college curriculum.

65 | Pa ge
11. ACTION PLAN TO ENHANCE BSCA GRADUATES' EMPLOYABILITY AT GORDON
COLLEGE
RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on the study and analysis of the answers of survey questionnaires and
feedback from the respondents, this study makes the following
recommendations:
 The employment status of graduates should be updated at least every three (3)
years to monitor and verify the results of the research.
 Establish an Online Alumni Tracking System. This will assist the academic
institution in keeping track of its alumni. It also enables alumni to communicate
with the institution via the internet.
 Future researchers ought to track as many graduates of Gordon College's
Bachelor of Science in Customs Administration as possible to obtain more
accurate outcomes.

CHALLENGES ENCOUNTERED AND COPING STRATEGIES OF CUSTOMS BROKER
PRACTICING AT SOME PORT
Rhea Jane A. Altares, Maricel A. Agan, Yvonne Q. Anulao, Juliene Gwyneth
J. Atazar, Ian P. Balingit, Ediric D. Gadia, Sherinne Angel Malong.
Gordon College, Olongapo City, Philippines
Abstract: The study aims to determine the relationship between challenges
encountered and coping strategies of Customs Brokers practicing in a certain
port located in Olongapo City, Philippines. The proponents decided to use a
mixed method as research design to achieve the study’s primary aim. The study
also utilized a purposive sample technique to gathered 40 respondents to
answer the survey questionnaires-via Google form. The proponents adopted
and modified an instrument in order to fit with the aims of the study and
subjected it to validity and reliability test. The study determined the challenges
and coping strategies using descriptive and inferential statistics with the help
of SPSS 23. Result shows that slow computer systems and computer system
breakdown were the primary challenges encountered by the practitioners. On
the other hand, customs broker seeks assistance from fellow customs broker
was the most effective and used coping strategy among the respondents. Finally,
the study also revealed a weak positive correlation between the challenges
encountered and the respondents’ coping strategies. In conclusion, there was a
weak relationship between the challenges encountered and the coping
strategies of the respondents. The researchers provided some recommendations
at the end of the study.
Keywords: Customs brokerage, Bureau of Customs, Freight forwarding, Import
and export, Work challenges, Coping strategies

69 | Pa ge
1. INTRODUCTION
Economic growth nowadays is primarily dependent on the dynamics of
international trade, which is where customs brokerage plays an important role.
Without it, importers and exporters who lack the time and knowledge of
customs rules and regulations would be unable to conduct business effectively.
The Philippine economy includes a significant percentage of the customs
brokerage sector. Communication between the government, importers, and
exporters is facilitated by it. A customs broker must hold a valid license in order
to deal with the Bureau of Customs on behalf of an importer or exporter.
Customs brokerage services provided in the Philippines include consultation,
preparation of import and export customs documentation, declaration and
payment of customs duties and taxes, and processing of import and export
entries (Republic Act No. 9280).
To fulfill the needs of international trade, customs brokerage services are
necessary due to the many requests from numerous clients. Customs brokers
find it challenging to steer clear of challenges when doing their duties, which
might result in customer resentment and shipment delays. Problems can also
occur as a result of client negligence, such as failing to submit or complete
necessary documents, unanticipated events like natural disasters and accidents
that delay the delivery of goods, and, occasionally, as a result of
misunderstandings and giving customs brokers too little time to complete their
work (Ermita et. al., 2016).
Customs brokers also face the challenge of meeting compliance and service
obligations while maintaining the costs required to deliver value to the market.
Global security concerns, economic uncertainty, and varying Customs and other
government agency approaches and processes represent true professional
challenges, as stated by Lorenze (2016).
In the study of Cuevas et al. (2018), the three most frequent issues customs
brokers run into are delays, damaged goods, and customs clearance. Customs
brokers also have a difficult time importing and exporting goods because they
must abide by the laws and regulations. They deal with a lot of uncertainty,
including current macrotrends. Additionally, they experience problems with
client negligence, communication with the importer, and document submission
problems (Lenari, 2013).
On the other hand, as stated by Sambayan (2014), the customs brokers
concurred that they have issues with incomplete documents, pending office
transactions, and low volumes of transactions. If left unattended, the challenges
they face could turn into a major issue for the entire process.
The transaction between the exporter or importer, customs broker, and
government agencies involved in keeping their goods moving through customs
and across borders, which is one of our country's significant sources of income,
would be impacted by the aforementioned problems. The researchers made the
decision to conduct this study as a result in order to offer solutions to the issues
they had identified.
The researchers chose to look into the challenges encountered and coping
mechanisms used by customs brokers practicing at the Port of Subic.
According to Republic Act No. 9280 otherwise known as the “Customs
Brokers Act of 2004”, licensed customs brokers are experts who focus on
offering services to importers and exporters. An importer or exporter engages a

70 | Pa ge
customs broker to represent him or her with the Bureau of Customs throughout
the process. Customs brokers assist clients with the preparation of necessary
documentation and/or electronic submissions, computation and payment of
taxes, duties, and excises, as well as facilitating interaction between importers
and exporters and governmental agencies.
The challenges raised by the customs brokers with whom the researchers
spoke in the Port of Subic, as well as prior studies on the same issue that they
had read, prompted the researchers to conduct this study. Issues concerning
import/export documentation, frequent changes in customs procedures, and
slow computer systems were discovered. To help future customs brokers
prepare for issues outlined in the survey, the researchers then want to identify
and provide solutions for the issues they discovered.
It would be tremendously helpful to have a foundation on the problems that
customs brokers in the Port of Subic encounter, as well as the coping strategies
they employ to cope with them, as BS Customs Administration students who
aim to become licensed customs brokers. Knowing the challenges, they face
would help them foresee issues and prevent them from occurring, as well as lay
the groundwork for developing workable solutions for more effective service
delivery.
2. RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
2.1 Research Design
The researchers used a mixed-methods research design. This approach aims
to integrate and blend qualitative and quantitative research approaches.
According to the Dovetail Editorial Team (2023), there are four different forms
of mixed-methods research design: convergent parallel, embedding,
explanatory sequential, and exploratory sequential. When analyzing the data in
this instance, the researchers employed the sequential explanatory design to
better explain the outcome. Lib Guides (2023), stated in their article that a
sequential explanatory design is a two-phase process that involves collecting
and analyzing quantitative data first, followed by collecting and analyzing
qualitative data based on the quantitative results. Additionally, they added that
the quantitative data is explained using the qualitative data. On the other hand,
the descriptive correlational research approach is used to explain the variables
and the correlations that naturally exist between and among them. It is used in
studies that display static representations of events and look for connections
between many parameters (Ivypanda, 2019).
To determine the challenges encountered by customs broker and their
coping techniques, the researchers used a variety of different research
methodologies. To better explain the quantitative and qualitative data, as well
as to find the connection between the two variables.
2.2 Treatment of Data
The data collected via Google form and hard copy were tallied and polished
using Microsoft Excel (2019) and then processed using statistical package for
social sciences (IBM-SPSS v.20). The following procedure were used:

71 | Pa ge
1. Percentage Frequency Distribution –used to determine the respondents’
profile in terms of age, sex, length of employment, nature of employment and
number of years transacting in the port of Subic.
2. Test of Normality – used to figure out whether the data had a normal
distribution or not in this instance, the researchers utilized the Shapiro-Wilk
test.
3. Weighted Mean – used to determine the difference of scope of practice and
challenges encountered as well as the coping strategies employed.
4. Pearson Product Moment of Correlation (Pearson - r) - used to examine the
link between the challenges experienced and the customs broker's coping
strategies.

Table 2 displays the challenges experienced by customs brokers. The overall
mean of 2.03 suggests that the obstacles were sometimes faced.
According to the findings, the most common challenges encountered by
customs brokers in their field of work were slow computer systems and
computer system breakdown. Both are rated as sometimes experienced, with a
total weighted mean score of 2.42. The e2m system in the Philippines has
experienced a computer slowdown due to processing numerous transactions
simultaneously, possibly due to the large number of users connected to the
internet provider.
According to Team T (2015), the computer program was improperly
designed and implemented, with no parallel or backup system. Customs brokers
in the Philippines have identified issues with the Terminal Appointment
Booking System (TABS), such as difficulty booking appointments due to a slow
computer system and unreliable internet connection. They also expressed
dissatisfaction with the inability to reach port operators via the contact

73 | Pa ge
information provided on the TABS website and the lack of documentation to
exempt trucks from TABS appointments.
As stated by Villotas (2014), customs forwarders and brokers have been
experiencing significant difficulties in clearing goods at customs, resulting in
significant losses for both importers and exporters. Most shipping lines and
forwarders have experienced issues with the recent e2m's implementation due
to system failures.
On the other hand, a computer system breakdown might be brought on by
dense data entry. The computer system might malfunction due to the volume of
encoded data. With regard to imports, several brokerage businesses had
problems, such as server failure when filing paperwork and problems with
confusing information stated. Their research demonstrates that these issues are
prevalent in businesses that engage in import-export operations. This results
from inadequate planning before system adoption (Cuevas et al., 2018).

achieving the desired goal, but it may also refer to the process of getting ready
for a strong launch toward a more desirable goal. According to Edison (2015),
a lot of unsuccessful individuals in life were on the verge of success when they

78 | Pa ge
use inefficient or low-level coping methods are more likely to fail than those
who use effective and high-level coping strategies. Gaps in coping skills impair
the ability to address problems and make sound judgments.

a decision is at the core of how an individual copes in a challenging scenario.

as problem solving and decision making by adopting coping methods. Learning
to ask why and how questions, as well as committing to learning the best
available information before making a decision or taking action, reduces the
chance of making a poor choice and making mistakes.

Part II: Qualitative findings of the study
Theme 1: Appropriate traits and professional character
The characteristics and personalities of individuals are subject to
variation based on their environment and the individuals with whom they
interact. In the presence of friends and family, an individual's behavior may be
inappropriate, peculiar, or humorous without consequence. However, in a
professional setting, an individual must exhibit only professionalism and
meritocracy to earn the respect and trust of their colleagues. The impact of
professionalism in the workplace is significant, as it not only enhances an
individual's performance but also that of their colleagues. Professionalism
fosters positivity and confidence, while also providing opportunities for skill
development, which can contribute to a successful career.
 Sub-theme: Learning from Mistakes
Regardless of an individual's professional status, it is inevitable that
mistakes will be made, as it is an inherent aspect of human life. A mistake is
defined as an incorrect action or decision caused by misunderstanding or
ignorance, which typically results in adverse consequences. Nevertheless,
mistakes can prove advantageous if individuals acknowledge and learn from
them. Furthermore, mistakes can serve as a valuable instrument for exploring
beyond our comfort zones, acquiring knowledge, attaining experience or even
just for personal development.
Theme 2: Essence of seeking advice
The essence of seeking advice lies in the recognition that no individual
possesses all the knowledge, experience, and perspective necessary to make the
best decisions in every situation. We seek advice from others or people who can
help us be more optimistic and think smarter to solve our problem, broaden our
thinking, or acquire a different perspective on our circumstances, which will
influence our decision-making. Additionally, seeking advice is vital because it

79 | Pa ge
enables us to venture outside of our comfort zones, view situations from a new
angle, and form more accurate judgments.
 Sub-theme: Essence of seeking assistance
In a society that frequently promotes self-sufficiency and independence,
the essence of seeking assistance is often neglected. Recognizing our limits and
embracing the potential of cooperation, we may seek assistance to tap into the
skills, knowledge, and resources of others to achieve our goals more effectively
and efficiently. It also entails that, by seeking assistance from others, no one
can do it all on their own. And by seeking assistance from others, we build our
thinking, which creates a drive to study and achieve more.
Theme 3: Proper execution of port protocol & process
Proper execution is critical to success, it is major factor to effectively
implement strategies, plans, policies and etcetera. The Protocol and Process are
an essential part of every organization, this aims to provide a framework that
guides people whether professional or not on how to perform certain tasks
effectively and efficiently in their certain fields. A well performed one will
result to a better-quality service, safer work place and a well organize system.
 Sub-theme: Preparation, process and procedures
Planning ahead make’s different events and situations run smoothly, well
organize and effectively. Having procedures and process to follow through is a
big factor just to make the flow of the organization outstanding and better.
Regardless of profession and different fields this approach helps all people to
enhance the quality of products and services as well as improve the reputation
of them or its organization.
Theme 4: Coping by problem solving
Coping strategies are strategies that are used in order to deal with
problems or stressful situations. Everyone is vulnerable to stress especially
those who are working. By approaching problems with a systematic and logical
mindset, problem-solving allows individuals to break down complex issues into
manageable parts and develop strategies to overcome them. This approach
promotes critical thinking, decision-making, and resilience, enabling
individuals to adapt and find solutions to various life challenges.
 Sub-theme: Personal reflection and coping mechanism
Personal reflection and coping mechanisms are both important in
overcoming challenges. Personal reflection helps to recognize one’s actions and
to better understand ourselves and our behaviors in a certain situation which
will serve as our self-awareness. While coping mechanism is a strategy
employed in order to overcome difficulties that are faced in a specific situation.

80 | Pa ge
INTEGRATION OF QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE FINDINGS
AND RESULTS
Figure 1. Emerging Conceptual Framework
Figure 1 reveals that customs brokers face various challenges, including
computer system failures and complexities in accomplishing crucial customs
forms. These difficulties not only affect clients but also the brokers themselves,
leading to delays in paperwork and transactions, and ungracious demands from
customers. This can challenge the professionalism of customs brokers.
Two significant challenges have been identified in order to substantiate the
quantitative findings of the study's narrative inquiry and thematic analysis. The
first problem revolves around possessing the appropriate traits and exhibiting a
professional demeanor. Customs brokers may encounter difficulties in
maintaining a professional attitude and demonstrating suitable attributes when
faced with obstacles such as delays, missing documentation, and demanding
clients. However, it is imperative that they effectively address these challenges
while upholding their professional image. By doing so, they can adeptly
overcome obstacles without conflict and prevent any substantial damage to their
career.
The second problem revolves around the proper execution of the Port
protocol and process. Most customs brokers find it difficult to follow the port
protocol and procedures. This difficulty may arise not only because the customs
broker is required to follow it, but also because other parties such as clients,
logistic partners, and other entities conducting indirect transactions with the
Bureau are also expected to adhere to the protocol. Failure to follow the
procedure and adhere to the port protocol by these parties may cause
inconvenience not only for the customs broker but also for the flow of the
transaction.

81 | Pa ge
Protocols play a crucial role in various domains of society, such as science,
technology, data communication, and business. Adhering to protocols and
procedures is imperative to ensure accurate task execution. According to Power
DMS (2020), employees who follow procedures and protocols perform tasks
correctly and provide consistent service to clients and customers. Additionally,
adhering to protocols and procedures not only enhances individuals' knowledge
and skills but also helps them build pride and a good reputation.
In addition to the previous challenge of adhering to port protocols and
procedures, issues pertaining to document preparation, processing, and customs
transaction procedures were identified as a challenge. A crucial duty of a
customs broker is to meticulously prepare and process the requisite documents
for business transactions with the bureau. However, for a customs broker to
effectively carry out this task, the client must initially furnish all the essential
information and documents.
According to Pregmon et al. (2023), effective document management and
control practices can significantly decrease the time and resources needed for
document preparation, while simultaneously preventing any potential issues
that may arise during the process. As stated by Cooks-Campbell (2022),
individuals should establish comprehensive plans to ensure proper document
preparation and contingency plans to address any unforeseen complications and
minimize the resulting inconvenience.
In terms of coping strategies, customs brokers seek assistance from fellow
customs brokers, particularly those who have been in the profession for many
years. Senior practitioners have more experience in the field and are expected
to have gained more and deeper knowledge about why challenges in the field
occur and how to solve and conquer these challenges.
Consulting with experienced individuals is a beneficial practice as it
provides a straightforward approach to acquiring knowledge and assists in
developing solutions to problems. Seeking advice from others allows
individuals to receive guidance and ideas simultaneously, which is akin to
accomplishing two tasks at once. Additionally, seeking assistance from people
they know opens up the possibility of receiving fresh ideas or a new perspective.
Based on the quantitative results, problem-solving was found to be a
valuable coping mechanism for customs brokers. This approach not only
addresses the problem at hand but also facilitates the development of optimal
solutions, as stated by the South Calgary Primary Care Network (2020). When
employed correctly, a problem-solving approach grants individuals a greater
sense of control and predictability over their problems.
Coping with personal reflection falls under the purview of this coping
strategy. Engaging in reflection enables individuals to enhance their
comprehension of the underlying factors contributing to a particular situation.
As stated by Herbert-Smith (2023), self-reflection empowers individuals to
move beyond mere experience and towards understanding. Moreover, personal
reflection fosters self-awareness and mindfulness regarding one's actions,
enabling the identification of areas for growth and areas of proficiency.

82 | Pa ge
CONCLUSIONS
Based on the findings generated from this study, the researchers made the
following conclusions:
1. The respondents are mostly male, with ages ranging from 30-39 years old
and most of them are serving in the industry for 1-5 years. Also, almost entirely
of the respondents are from the private sector. Furthermore, the majority of the
respondents have been transacting in the port of Subic mostly for 1-5 years as
well.
2. Based on the result, the most frequent challenges encountered by the customs
broker in the Port of Subic were (1) Slow computer systems, (2) Computer
system breakdown, and (3) Lack of material time to meet the import/export
commitments. While on the other hand, the least challenge encountered was
inadequate working facilities. Moreover, other challenges were stated by the
respondents with which difficulties in completing required documents are listed
as the most frequent.
3. In the matter of coping strategies, the (1) customs broker seeks assistance
from fellow customs broker, and (2) When a customs broker encounters a
challenge at work, he or she does not give up easily; instead, he/she continues
to try to solve it were generally used by the respondents based on the outcome
of the results. Additionally, the customs broker tried to forget the bad things
that happened as a result of the work challenges he/she faced and carried on as
if nothing had happened was the most uncommon coping strategy used by the
respondents. Furthermore, the other coping strategies indexed by the
respondents were (1) The customs broker communicates with other customs
brokers or processors to seek advice or help, and (2) The customs broker is
completing and preparing documents on time or ahead of schedule which are
the most prevalent.
4. According to the findings, the researchers conclude that there is a weak
positive correlation between the challenges encountered and coping strategies.
According to thematic analysis, two major challenges were identified:
executing appropriate traits and professional character and adhering to port
protocol and procedure. In terms of coping strategies, two major things were
discovered: coping through problem solving and seeking advice.
RECOMMENDATIONS
Following a thorough examination of the study’s findings and conclusions,
the following recommendations are presented:
1. The study's findings were limited to customs brokers working in the Port of
Subic. It is recommended that the research not be limited to respondents from
one or two ports; if feasible, all ports in the Philippines should be covered. This
aims to collect data from customs brokers in various ports around the
Philippines, as well as to examine the disparities in the degree of challenges
they face, as well as the coping techniques they adopt based on the
location/ports where they practice customs brokerage.
2. It is recommended that licensed customs brokers engage in CPD, or
Continuing Professional Development, especially if they have worked in the
field for five years or more. This will help them greatly in reviewing and
updating their professional knowledge and skills that they can use to keep up
with changes in the customs brokerage industry.

83 | Pa ge
3. It is recommended that seminars should be held for both regular and new
importers/clients. This is to help them better understand the system and
processes involved in the import-export trade industry.
4. The researchers also recommend improving internet quality and computer
system by updating and upgrading their tools and system for technological
advancement in accordance with the Bureau of Customs objective of
computerizing and modernizing manual processes supporting Electronic to
Mobile System and shall focus through ICT related activities.
5. It is recommended that future researcher re-study the same topic from the
same place to see whether there has been development in the mechanisms
implemented in the import-export trading industry and the performance of
licensed customs brokers. In addition, the same research should be conducted
from the standpoint of freight forwarding and customs brokerage businesses.

Introduction
The Gordon College-College of Computer Studi es Computing Research Journal (GC CCS CRJ)
is an official publication of the College of Compu ter Studies featuring research studies conducted
by faculty members and students for Academic Years 2019-2021 under the BS Computer Science
and BS Information Technology programs. The featured studies in this journal have been
presented to national and regional research conferences and have received recognition from
CHED, UP and ALCU for best research presentation. This journal showcases the extraordinary
work of students and faculty members in conducting research focusing on the development and
implementation of software solutions that addres s the needs of users across multiple sectors such
as business, education, government and local co mmunity.
The global pandemic has brought challenges and disruption in the education sector. However, the
College of Computer Studies continues to develop innovative research studies that enabled our
school to deliver continuity of the teaching and learning process. We would like to highlight a
study featured in this journal entitled: GC LAMP that served as the inspiration for the R3LAMP
project that aims to provide a free learning man agement system for higher education institutions
in Region 3 with CHED Region 3 at its primary beneficiary. This project, funded by DOST, is a
collaboration among the students and faculty members of the College of Computer Studies as part
of its research and community extension programs.
It is our hope that through this journal, our readers will be enthused by the opportunities that the
field of computing offers especially in software development. We hope that the same current and
emerging technologies that the studies contained herein utilized will also be the same technologies
that our readers will use in their future resear ches. We look forward for your projects to be
featured in this journal with emphasis in the areas of data science, machine learning, cloud
computing and mobile application development.
Thank you for your interest in this journal and we hope that you enjoy reading! Let's make
Intelligent Things happen!

5. CONCLUSION
The GC LAMP was developed to the have a simpler, more
rapid and easier platform for the retrieval of the educational
materials of the students. The Gordon College Learners’
Academic Management Portal reduces time and effort for
distributing learning materials and provides students access to
knowledge even outside of the classroom.
6
Based on the features of the study, the following objectives
of GC LAMP have all been achieved:
1. Reduce expenses by providing an online platform to aid
distance learning to continue monitoring student’s academic
performance on remote teaching.
2. Provide a centralized repository of learning materials in
different formats that users can access and share at anytime
and anywhere
3. Encouraged engagement between students and faculty despite
of not being physically present.
4. Provide a platform to announce news and reliable source of
information about the institution.

8. CONCLUSION
In conclusion, the project is in its continuous development,
and the potential that it offers will surely help consumers to have
safe, healthy and worth value of food that the mobile application
can offer. It certainly opens business opportunities to house
wives who can cook, the unemployed or employed individuals
who have passion in cooking, students who can create new
dishes, and grandparents who keep the secrets of traditional and
cultural food preparations of the Philippines and International
cuisines. Part of the tripartite relationship, motor riders, tricycle
drivers and license student drivers can also benefit on this
project income by managing the delivery process of the project
to earn.
Every start-up business idea entails risk in its implementa-
tion and putting up a traditional business orientation requires too
much capital and exerted effort. Therefore, the vision of this
project is to provide people with possible business opportunities,
match and recommend them to certain clients who want their
services in cooking and in delivery.
The validation made sets the direction and inspiration of
this project to progress as the acceptability rating for this mobile
application has already been set to high.

well on Linux, Mac and Windows. Since most actual web server
deployments use the same components as XAMPP, it makes
transitioning from a local test server to a live server extremely
easy as well.

After considering all the studies, the proponent therefore
concludes that this Cross-Platform Barangay Complaint
Management and Confrontation Scheduling Application for
Barangay New Kalalake will help each members of the
community:
A. For the Barangay constituents to:
1. Lessen their time consumed to file a complaint.
2. Get an immediate response for their confrontation schedule
assessment and be notified immediately after setting a
schedule for them.
3. Monitor their complaint status and to make easy way for
directly sending their concerns for be totally apprehended by
the Barangay Officials.
B. For the Barangay Officials to:
1. Organize each complaint files according to its complaint
status, and manage the distribution of confrontation
schedule for each complaint.
Figure 21. Mobile Application – Terms and Policy Page
2. Know the available dates and time that they can
accommodate confrontation by viewing the full calendar
feature of the application.
3. Generate easily their required reports such as monthly report
that the Barangay needs to submit to the Hall of Justice and
narrative reports for their documentation and validation
purposes.
4. Increase the Barangay’s productivity and to make their work
easily, fast and accurate.

In conclusion, the project is in its continuous development
but the potential that it offers will surely benefit both the
travelers and the resort, hotels, adventure parks, water parks
owners. By encouraging and attracting travelers to visit different
destinations, tourism businesses can gain more customers. And

75% of businesses agreed to subscribe to the application to be

willing to take challenges. These are enough for them to envision
that this solution will be successful. For future development, the
developers have plans to apply augmented reality for collecting
badges so that it will be more interesting to use. They also have
plans to have character that a user can customize and dress up.
Tara G! is currently in its development, but its beta version is
already available and can be downloaded in Google Play.

in the world to sustain and produce good communication and connect with others. It has a huge impact on the community and
people use gadgets and machines so work will be done in a fast pace, easier and more convenient way. According to Vladimir Z
(1996), that electronic commerce (E-commerce) is sharing business information, maintaining business relationships, and
conducting business transactions by means of telecommunication networks and doing business over the internet, selling goods
and services which are delivered offline as well as products which can be “digitized” and delivered online, such as computer
software. In short, it is the buying, selling, and exchanging products, services, and goods over on the internet. The proponent had
conducted research regards to ecommerce, studies about the problem and conducted interviews and gathered surveys online. The
study was concerned with marketing the books online or buy it personally if the publisher/store can never be sure when books are
sold and purchase takes ages meanwhile for customers, most of them they bought books once, mostly buying books with romance
genre, dissatisfied with its quality and finding reliable and legit sellers so that they will buy their desired book. The proponent
proposed a system entitled proposed A Local Book Android Based Online Shopping in Olongapo City Using Collaborative
Filtering Recommendation Algorithm. The project is an application that helps buyers to browse and seek for their best-loved and
dearest book item while sellers posting their new or used books from nearby places in Olongapo City.
DAWN WOODS: A 2D Android Adventure Indie Game for the Android Phone
Arnie D. Armada and Linkel Rae L. Lee
Dawn Woods – A 2D Android Adventure game is an android application design for gamers who want to experience an exciting
game that survive a brutality obstacle along the quest and mysteries of the woods. It is an application available in Google Play
Store. Dawn Woods is a game that has two-mode, survival mode and story mode survival mode is a type of game in which the
player must continue playing for as long as possible without dying in an uninterrupted session while the game presents them with
increasingly difficult waves of challenges. And story mode turn-based game that will focus on protagonist adventure encounter in
different places. The story mode is a continuing storyline or set of adventures, typically involving the same characters. Dawn
Woods was developed to be a 2D mobile game application for Android. The application was created using the development tools
such as Unity 3D as the game engine, Aseprite for creating the characters, and Adobe Photoshop for designing the background,
buttons and logos. The system had undergone testing through conformance and compatibility test. The result of the test was used
to improve the systems over-all performance. The evaluation was conducted to achieve the system’s acceptance of the user based
from the Android Core App Quality standards using the criteria such as Visual Design and User Interaction, Functionality,
Performance and Stability and Google Play. The evaluation instrument used was based from the Android Game Application and
participated by ten (10) IT Experts and thirty (30) mobile-users. The result garnered an overall mean of 2.85‖ and standard deviation
of 0.63‖ with an interpretation of Fairly Acceptable‖ which meant that the system could be played and provided insights about the
Dawn Woods. Dawn Woods has many environments in the games in the Woods, River, Circus and many events places of the story
of the characters. The Woods is the started it all that when the car accident started and the disappearance of the lost sister and
badges where the character can collect achievement, it’s also consist of dangerous obstacle that can be seen in woods like spike
and bats. The River consist of moving waters while dodging all obstacle to reach the end of the level. The Circus has spike and
cars that can ride while running to avoid the dangerous obstacle to reach the end of the levels.
Ebudgetmo: A Competitive Android Mobile Based Budgeting Tracker Application
Using Ionic Framework
Tricia Mae M. Gayatin
My project entitled Ebudgetmo: A Competitive Android Mobile Based Tracker Budgeting Application using Ionic
Framework is an application that will change the perspective in budgeting. It is a budgeting application with a little fun on the
side. It brings the excitement in budgeting. Not everyone has the capability to manage their funds on hand. Some might look it as
an inferior skill, especially if you do not take into consideration all the cash inflows and outflows. We have this habit of counting
the chicks before the eggs hatched resulting to cash mismanagement and regretting after we see the consequences of mismanaged
decisions. Budgeting is the process of creating a plan to spend your money. This spending plan is called a budget. Creating this
spending plan allows you to determine in advance whether you will have enough money to do the things you need to do or would
like to do. If you don't have enough money to do everything you would like to do, then you can use this planning process to
prioritize your spending and focus your money on the things that are most important to you. Since budgeting allows you to create
a spending plan for your money, it ensures that you will always have enough money for the things you need and the things that
are important to you. Following a budget or spending plan will also keep you out of debt or help you work your way out of debt
if you are currently in debt. Budgeting is simply balancing your expenses with your income. If they don't balance and you spend
more than you make, you will have a problem. Many people don't realize that they spend more than they earn and slowly sink
deeper into debt every year. This application will help almost everyone because the layout and design are user-friendly.

IMPACT OF COMPUTER-ASSISTED INSTRUCTION (CAI) TO THE BSED-SCIENCE
STUDENTS’ ENGAGEMENT AND LEARNING EXPERIENCES AMIDST
COVID-19 PANDEMIC
Kristoffer Paul C. Obispo1
Jason M. Yap1
Froiland Caliboso1
Mica Daireen Niduaza1
Rheena Janelle Udan1
1College of Education, Arts, and Sciences
ABSTRACT
This study determined the impact of Computer-Assisted Instruction (CAI) on students’
learning experiences and engagement amidst COVID-19. A descriptive research method
was utilized. It was revealed that CAI tools improve teacher-student communication and
the students’ learning outcomes. There was a significant difference in students’ learning
experiences in terms of Faculty-Student interaction, student content, and Student
Character when grouped according to Year Level and Age. In Faculty-Student Interaction,
the learning experiences of 3rd-year students from age bracket of 18-20 significantly differ
from 1st and 2nd year and from 21 and above age group, respectively. In terms of student
content, students from the age group of 18-20 significantly differ from students under 21
and above. In Student Character, the learning experiences of 1st and 2nd year and from
18-20 age group are better than those of the 3rd year students and from the age group
of 21 and above, respectively. Additionally, there were significant differences in the
students’ engagement when grouped according to year level and age. The study
recommends conducting CAI Training Programs further to capacitate the instructors, as
well as students, to improve the teaching-learning process despite the implementation of
Distance Learning due to COVID-19.
Keywords: Computer-Assisted Instruction, Learning Experiences, Students’
Engagement, COVID-19, Behavioral Engagement, Cognitive Engagement, Affective
Engagement
How to cite: Obispo, K.P.C., Yap, J.M., Caliboso, F., Niduaza, M.D., Udan, R.J. (2022). Impact of computer-
assisted instruction (CAI) to the BSEd-Science students’ engagement and learning experiences amidst
COVID-19 pandemic. The APO, 5(1), 77-97. https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.10799079
INTRODUCTION
The COVID-19 pandemic has altered the course of history. Due to the nature of the virus,
residents were instructed to stay at home and non-essential establishments, public
transportation, malls, and even schools and universities were closed. This greatly affected
77

THE APO
Volume 5, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
the delivery of quality education to the students as face-to-face interaction and traditional
classroom settings were prohibited. Higher education institutions (HEIs), both public and
private, have also had to adjust to the new situation by finding innovative ways to pursue
education, research, and service (Simbulan, 2020). To address the situation, the
Commission on Higher Education (CHEd) implemented Flexible Learning to ensure the
continuity of inclusive and accessible education. Flexible learning is a pedagogical
strategy that allows for time, place, and audience flexibility, including, but not limited to,
the use of technology.
Though CHEd and the Department of Education (DepEd) have already pursued the
integration of Information and Communications Technology (ICT) in the school curriculum
(Dap-og, Orongan, 2021) before the pandemic, the course syllabus and requirements
were transitioned to flexible teaching and learning modalities which made the students
and teachers heavily relied more on the use of ICT. This ICT has been integrated into a
variety of ways in the teaching-learning process, such as Computer Assisted Instruction
(CAI), to facilitate students’ learning (Dap-og, Orongan, 2021).
Among other disciplines, science requires a lot of visualizations and experiments. Due to
the situation, teaching science to students has become a challenge. Virtual laboratory
simulation websites, software and other computer applications have been used as CAI
tools in providing activities to represent abstract ideas. Physics Education Technology
(PhET), Amrita Virtual Laboratories, interactive PowerPoint presentations, and video
lectures are just some of these CAI tools. Several studies have provided evidence of
CAI’s effectiveness in instruction in promoting students’ interest and academic
achievement (Chinwendu & Patience, 2017).
There are four interactions necessary for effective online education which was adopted
from Moore’s Transactional Distance Theory, which explains that "distance education is
not just a geographic separation of students and professors; it is, more crucially, a
pedagogical concept (Culatta, 2018). These interactions include Faculty-student,
Student-content, Student-student, and Student Character, which were used in this study
to describe the learning experiences of the students. Students’ engagement, on the other
hand, was also categorized into three dimensions: Behavioral, Affective, and Cognitive.
Interaction between instructors and learners is a critical element in the learning process
during an online course. In the context of online education, effective teacher-student
interaction is a prerequisite for deep learning, according to other researchers as well (Mu
& Wang, 2019); it is the most important aspect of the online learning environment (Jiang,
et al., 2019). Moore (1989) defined student-content interaction as “the process of
intellectually interacting with content that results in changes in the learner’s
understanding, the learner’s perspective or the cognitive structures of the learner’s mind”
and characterized it as “the defining characteristic of education.” In a traditional classroom
set-up, student-student interaction occurs face-to-face. However, in online distance
learning, this type of interaction occurs digitally or virtually through email, instant
messaging applications, and various social media platforms and even in virtual
simulations. According to the study conducted by Nwanko (2015), one variable of
transactional distance that influences students’ learning experiences is the personalities
78

THE APO
Volume 5, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
of students themselves and an important component of personality for distance learners
is autonomy or the ability to work independently.
The concept of engagement is frequently used in education to explain a range of actions
that students take in the classroom. According to researchers, the notion of student
engagement is still vague and there isn't a clear consensus on how to assess it.
(Boekaerts, 2016). Fredricks et al. (2004) typology of student engagement suggests that
there are three types of engagement: Behavioral, Cognitive, and Affective or Emotional.
According to the National Association of Social Workers Press and Oxford University
Press, behavioral theory seeks to explain human behavior by analyzing the antecedents
and consequences present in the individual's environment and the learned associations
he or she has acquired through previous experience (Angell, 2013). According to
Fredricks et al. (2004), behavioral engagement refers to a student's actions while
completing a learning assignment, including their effort, persistence, and contribution to
their own learning. Recent research has characterized behavioral engagement as student
involvement, effort, attention, persistence, and positive behavior toward the learning
activity (Fredricks et al., 2016). Second, the affective theory of mind has three
subcomponents of executive functions (inhibition, updating, and shifting). Affective theory
of mind was positively related to age, and all three executive functions (Vetter, 2013).
Student involvement is influenced by a number of affective factors, such as attitude,
personality, motivation, effort, and self-confidence (Mandernach et al., 2011).
By evaluating the level of student engagement and considering these affective aspects,
instructors can more effectively plan lessons and activities that will encourage students
to be more active participants in their learning and coursework (Jennings & Angelo, 2006;
Mandernach et al., 2011). Then, Cognitive theories of multimedia learning tend to focus
on instructional methods aimed at reducing extraneous processing. While motivational
theories frequently concentrate on instructional strategies designed to promote
generative processing, they tend to place less emphasis on managing necessary
processing (such as splitting a lesson into sections) or managing essential content. (such
as adding appealing graphics or challenging scenarios) (Mayer, 2014). Cognitive
engagement is defined as the students’ level of investment in learning; it includes being
thoughtful and purposeful in the approach to school tasks and being willing to exert the
effort necessary to comprehend complex ideas or master difficult skills (Fredricks, 2004).
Cognitive engagement includes thinking deeply and broadly about concepts while using
strategies such as organization, rehearsal, and elaboration as well as regulating and
managing the learning process (Hidayah et al., 2021)
Hence, this study was conducted to describe the impact of Computer Assisted Instruction
to the learning experiences and engagement of 1st, 2nd and 3rd year students from the
Bachelor of Secondary Education- Major in Science amidst the pandemic.
RESEARCH METHODOLOGY
Research Design
This study used the descriptive method of research. A descriptive study systematically
describes the facts and characteristics of a given population or those that are of interest,
79

THE APO
Volume 5, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
factually and accurately (Bueno, 2006). It is concerned with the conditions or relationships
that exist, opinions that are held, processes that are going on, effects that are evident, or
trends that are developing (Best & Kahn, 2009). The purpose of this study is to collect
information that describes existing phenomena; identify problems or justify current
conditions and practices, and make comparisons and evaluations (Bueno, 2006). The
methodology used in this study is the survey research. Survey research obtains data to
determine and summarize the specific characteristics of individuals or groups or physical
environments (Fraenkel & Wallen, 2012). Here, the researchers used a survey
questionnaire to collect data and to assess the impact of Computer-Assisted Instruction
on the BSEd-Science Students’ Learning Experiences and Engagement. This involves
asking the same set of questions to the chosen respondents via Google Forms. Thus, the
main purpose and reason of the study is to determine the impact of Computer-Assisted
Instruction on the BSEd-Science students’ learning experiences and engagement.
Respondents
The respondents of this study were the BSEd-Science 1st, 2nd, and 3rd-year students,
who are currently enrolled at Gordon College, Olongapo City for the Academic Year 2021-
2022. The researchers used non-probability sampling. Non-probability sampling is a
sampling procedure that will not bid a basis for any opinion of probability that elements in
the universe will have a chance to be included in the study sample (Etikan & Bala, 2017).
In particular, the non-probability sampling used in the study was purposive sampling.
Purposive sampling is when a researcher chooses respondents based on their personal
viewpoint of who will be the most representative or useful (Polit and Beck, 2006). The
researchers may choose individuals who are thought to be representative of the general
population or who are particularly knowledgeable about the issues under research. In this
study, the researchers believe that the students of Bachelor of Secondary Education-
Major in Science were suitable respondents for the research as they were exposed to
Computer-Assisted Instruction which includes the utilization of virtual laboratory
simulations and video lectures during the implementation of Flexible Learning. The
researchers ensure that the participants possess the desired information and that they
are all willing to answer the questions.
Validation of the Instrument
To ensure the reliability of the instrument, the questionnaire was validated by the
experts, specifically the teachers engaged in teaching Science and Research courses,
and piloted to 30 students from the College of Education, Arts and Sciences in Gordon
College. Pilot testing was done to test the research approach with a small number of
participants before conducting the main study (Wright & So, 2022). This aims to improve
some of the items in the instrument. It will be judged if the questionnaire is fully
understood and accepted based on the results of the dry run.
The data gathered from the pilot testing was statistically treated to generate Cronbach
alpha values to measure the internal consistency and reliability of the Likert Scale
questions. Results of the reliability test indicated “Acceptable” (0.772) Cronbach’s alpha
values for: Faculty-Student (0.700, Acceptable), Student-Content (0.701, Acceptable),
80

THE APO
Volume 5, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
Student-Content (0.904, Excellent), Student Character (0.762, Acceptable), Behavioral
Engagement (0.772, Acceptable), Cognitive Engagement (0.831, Good), and Affective
Engagement (0.734, Acceptable).
The experts' comments were also taken into account. Before administering the final draft
of questionnaires, the revised instrument was sent to the adviser for feedback and
suggestions.
Statistical Analysis
The study underwent statistical analysis with the aid of SPSS 20. The statistical tools
used in the computation were frequency, percentage, and mean for the descriptive part.
For the inferential statistics, the study used t-test and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA).

interpretation to answer specific problems posited. It includes the profile of the
respondents, most used CAI Tools and differences of the variables and the implications
of the learning experiences and students’ engagement on Computer-Assisted Instruction
(CAI).

affected by their exploration of technology applications (Mahmood, 2006).

technologies they had reviewed (Web-conferencing, Blogs, Wikis, Facebook, Twitter, and
Digital Games) had a positive influence on multiple indicators of student engagement. For
instance, digital games influence all three types of student engagement. First, digital
games were designed to provide authentic learning contexts in which students could

higher competence belief regarding learning in digital settings in young women compared
to young men. Furthermore, it has been found that individuals high on both masculinity
and femininity—androgynous individuals—are more flexible and adaptable to different
situations, as they possess a broader repertoire of traits and behaviors (Pauletti et al.,

A study conducted by Simonds and Brock (2014) showed that different age groups
respond differently to online learning methods, which can also be supported by Morin et
al. (2019), where older students found asynchronous forms of learning such as pre-
recorded video lectures to be useful learning activities and younger students preferred
interactive learning, such as; live chats and group projects. Koh and Lim (2012) reported
a similar finding for younger students in their study. Also, offering older students a blend
of synchronous and asynchronous activities in a course will appeal to their comfort level
while also exposing them to new ways of learning. Younger students will also benefit from
this blended approach as they learn how to use digital tools for the purpose of academic
learning (Simonds & Brock, 2014).
Age is certainly an important factor to consider when designing online courses. Morin et
al. (2019) revealed that students in the older category are more enthusiastic about
participating in online learning as they feel that they have stronger self-efficacy and better
mental readiness. In this regard, course designers and instructors are suggested to
design effective online teaching strategies that can be used with any age group and
execute the course considering the ease of use and guided pedagogy implemented in the
online learning website with dynamic and interactive activities that connect students to
students to teachers to content (Morin et al., 2019).

These findings might be associated with the postponement of science courses which
were supposedly done on a face-to-face set-up such as practical laboratory works and

COVID-19, this resulted in the lack of motor skills experiences, less chance of direct
consultation with the instructors, and less practical assignments (Amir et al., 2020) that
can lead to students being less engaged.
The study of Avila et al. (2021), conducted at the time of the COVID-19 Pandemic,
showed that freshmen students perceived that distance learning is good and is necessary
for their degrees and despite the sudden shift in the teaching modalities from the
traditional classroom setup, the students often utilize educational technologies as they
are often motivated to join their online classes.
In a study by Amir et al. (2020), among dental students who preferred distance learning,
the percentage of freshman students was significantly higher than the of seniors.
According to Amir et al. (2020), one factor that contributes to this finding might be related
to the curriculum implemented at the time of the study. Senior students learned more
courses that involve both theory and procedural knowledge and skills which essentially
required laboratory skill sessions to enhance the understanding of the learned subjects.
The curriculum of first-year students studied more basic science courses which are mostly
conceptual theories so that the content knowledge acquisition could still be reinforced by
laboratory activities based on online tutorials and exercises in the form of videos or
photographs. However, it was also revealed that more students felt lower learning
satisfaction and more difficulty communicating either with instructors or with peer students
during distance learning due to COVID-19.

Age is often associated with a decline in cognitive abilities (Clark et al., 2015). The study
of Amir et al. (2014) found a significant difference in the three levels of engagement
between students of different age groups. Their study revealed that students’
engagement decreases as they grow older. Particularly, their data showed that as
students grow older, their cognitive participation in class activity declines, which is in line
with the results of the current study. The study suggested that teachers are supposed to
be trained to learn how to give attention to all students regardless of their genders or
ages.
CONCLUSION
Based on the findings, the following conclusions were drawn:
● The majority of BSEd-Science students are aged 18-20, use mobile data, and own
a PC/laptop.
● The most frequently used CAI (Computer-Assisted Instruction) tools among these
students are Google Meet, Google Classroom, GCLAMP, and PowerPoint
Presentations. For virtual laboratory simulations, Amrita and PhET simulations are
the top choices.
● Students' experiences with CAI indicate a preference for instructors using CAI over
traditional methods, attributing to better teacher-student communication. CAI tools
enhance memory recall, understanding, creativity, and competitiveness, promoting
group activities. They also encourage self-driven learning, punctuality, flexibility,
and efficiency.
● With respect to engagement, students are more attentive, undistracted, and
proactive during CAI-based classes. They can relate content to real-life scenarios
and are comfortable using various CAI tools. Most respondents are emotionally
engaged during these sessions.
● Students' CAI learning experiences vary based on year level and age, especially
in terms of faculty-student and student-content interactions. However, factors like
92

THE APO
Volume 5, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
Sex, Internet Connectivity, and Computer Ownership don't significantly affect their
experiences.
● Engagement levels among students, categorized by Sex, Year Level, and Age,
showed mixed results. Year Level affected behavioral engagement, Age
influenced cognitive engagement, while both Year Level and Age impacted
affective engagement. Sex had minimal influence on engagement metrics.
RECOMMENDATION
Based on the findings and conclusions, the following are recommended:
1. The College Administration and instructors should utilize the result of this study by
giving full identification and understanding of the student’s engagement and
learning experiences from CAI to help them design innovative classroom activities
and strategies to improve the teaching-learning process further.
2. Gordon College Instructors, as well as students, should continue attending to
available Computer-related Training Programs to keep abreast with the latest
trends and innovations in teaching and learning.
3. The government should take advantage of the respondents’ and instructors’
enthusiasm to bring technology into the classroom by providing them with the
necessary tools and greater access to CAI-infused training programs.
4. Assistance should be extended to students who wish to acquire a personal
computer or laptop to help build basic computer competence and ICT pedagogical
skills.
5. Related research should be conducted to build on this study and examine the
students’ perception of CAI in learning Science, as well as their preferences and
responses to the utilization of various CAI tools in the classroom.
6. Do more exploration regarding the topic further to enhance the validity and
reliability of the study.

FACTORS AFFECTING PHYSICAL WELLNESS AMONG TERTIARY STUDENT
IN GORDON COLLEGE
Louise D. Giron1, LPT
1College of Education, Arts, and Sciences
ABSTRACT
Physical wellness is a crucial component of a student's overall well-being and significantly
impacts how well they do in school and how happy they are. To understand the difficulties,
they encounter and possible solutions, this study explores the many elements that affect
the physical wellness of Gordon College's tertiary students. The study found several
important elements that impacted Gordon College tertiary students' physical welfare.
Physical activity was a key factor, and students who exercise regularly reported feeling
physically better. The importance of dietary habits was discovered, and a balanced diet
and enough water consumption are favorably correlated with well-being.
Keywords: Physical Wellness, Exercise, Factors, Height, Weight, Body Mass Index
(BMI)
How to cite: Giron, L.D. (2022). Factors affecting physical wellness among tertiary student in Gordon
College. The APO, 5(1), 43-60. https://zenodo.org/doi/10.5281/zenodo.10795811
INTRODUCTION
College Students contributions to an Institution are highly significant factors in school
performance. College Students must maintain academic standing associated with time
management to continue their academic career (Macan et al.,1990). However, because
of this pressure, the students experience various stressors such as yearly tuition fees,
academic competition, tons of requirements, time management, and personal issues
(Neibling & Heckert 1999; Fogle & Pettijohn, 2013). These stressors may lead to extreme
amounts of stress over a long period of time. Stress is often described as a feeling of
being overwhelmed, worried, or run down. Stress can affect people of all ages, genders,
and circumstances and can lead to both physical and psychological health issues.
College students cannot really find the time to exercise because of loaded requirements,
feeling tired, and lack of time (Reichert et al., 2005). The nature of this dedication required
to manage such demanding schedules, along with the growing health benefits of physical
activity (Darren, 2006).
As a result, most of the students have physical inactivity or “sitting disease” that leads to
slower blood flow, the feeling of fatigue, and risk for diabetes, chronic back pain, and risk
of heart attack (Hoeger et al., 2017; Pajović et al.,2014). Furthermore, regular exercise
43

THE APO
Volume 5, Issue 1
The Official Research Journal of January to December 2022
Gordon College ISSN: 2546-1745
can improve sleep patterns, and immune function, reduce mental stress and anxiety, and
most importantly, treat mild and moderate depression.
Kennedy, (2013) suggests that “physical fitness” is not only the most important key to a
healthy body; it is the basis of dynamic and “creative intellectual” activity.
Another problem that occurs among college students is their unhealthy lifestyle (Brunt &
Rhee, 2008).
College students affect their dietary habits negatively when they are away from the family
(Brunt & Rhee, 2008). In the same manner, Dr. Augusto Litonjua, president of the
Philippine Center for Diabetes Education Foundation blamed the “fast-food culture” for
offering calorie-dense food, which leads to obesity and a higher risk for diabetes.
This undertaking might make it possible to know the factors affecting the physical
wellness among college students at Gordon College.
The researcher aims to investigate the significance of differences when grouped based
on demographic factors namely: age, sex, height, weight, body mass index (BMI), and
College Department.
Review of Related Literature
Increased implementation of technology will increase students' comprehension of content
and the development of skills in such areas as analytical reasoning, problem-solving,
information evaluation, and creative thinking. In KSA, there is a dire dearth and paucity
of information regarding the effect of technology usage on learning achievement. Rather,
studies conducted within KSA have found that students are used to a comparatively more
traditional learning model. However, the comprehensive use of technology would create
a good environment that facilitates of learning. This approach would shift education from
the classical approach (which has not prioritized students' pursuit of understanding)
toward the deep-meaning approaches that would help students seek a true understanding
of the central principles, themes, and applications of any given area of study. Using
technology would support the active learning of students in an educational environment
designed to help students achieve meaningful learning – which, in turn, could result in
positive, cumulatively progressive gains in learning outcomes (Al-Hariri & Al-Hattami,
2017).
Compared to students who lived off-campus, those who lived on campus consumed a
larger variety of fruits, vegetables, and dairy products. Those who lived off-campus
consumed less variety of grains compared to those who lived with parents (Brunt & Rhee,
2008). There are a variety of predictors of obesity including genetics, physical activity,
and food consumption and there are other outcomes of food choice and nutrition that also
have an independent effect on health including some types of cancer, cardiovascular
disease, and diabetes (Deshpande et al, 2009).
The present study examined perceived stress, health habits, and daily hassles and uplifts
among 135 college freshmen. We hypothesized that students with lower stress levels
would be male, would have better self-care health habits, would experience fewer minor
medical health issues, would have higher academic performance, and would experience
fewer daily hassles and more daily uplifts than students who experienced high perceived
stress (Fogle, 2013).
